item.title: Goolsbee, do Fed: manter inflação alta por tanto tempo é “brincar com fogo”
item.description: O presidente do Federal Reserve de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmou nesta terça-feira que permitir que a inflação permaneça acima da meta do Fed por 5 anos e meio é “brincar com fogo”, observando que o Fed pode precisar responder a um choque de oferta com efeitos de longo prazo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Federal Reserve de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmou nesta terça-feira que permitir que a inflação permaneça acima da meta do Fed por 5 anos e meio é “brincar com fogo”, observando que o Fed pode precisar responder a um choque de oferta com efeitos de longo prazo. “É uma situação desagradável... (mas) acho que temos que considerar a possibilidade de responder a esses choques persistentes”, disse Goolsbee. Ele afirmou ser um dos formuladores de políticas mais otimistas do Fed no que diz respeito às suas expectativas sobre a trajetória das taxas, mas, antes de reduzir as taxas, “precisamos ter alguma evidência de que a inflação está voltando a cair, de que essas situações que deveriam ser temporárias estão, de fato, desaparecendo”.

item.title: Two-time NBA champ J.R. Smith arrested on assault charge
item.description: Two-time NBA champion J.R. Smith was arrested on a charge of family violence in Texas on Monday, according to multiple reports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two-time NBA champion J.R. Smith was arrested on a charge of family violence in Texas on Monday, according to multiple reports. No bond had been set and Smith, 41, remained behind bars at the Hunt County Detention Center as of midday on Tuesday, according to jail records. Smith was arrested by the Royse City Police Department on a warrant issued by the Southlake Police Department for a charge of assault causing bodily injury family violence. Police did not release any further details. Smith was arrested by the Royse City Police Department on a warrant issued by police in Southlake, Texas, for a charge of family violence assault causing bodily injury. Police did not release any further details. Smith, a 6-foot-6 shooting guard, won NBA championships with the Cleveland Cavaliers (2015-16) and Los Angeles Lakers (2019-20) during a 16-year career with five teams. The 2012-13 Sixth Man of the Year averaged 12.4 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 977 career games (395 starts) with the New Orleans Hornets, Denver Nuggets, New York Knicks, Cavaliers and Lakers. The Hornets drafted him in the first round (18th overall) in 2004. --Field Level Media

item.title: Williams no ve urgencia para próxima alza de tasas de la Fed
item.description: El presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams, afirmó el martes que el banco central estadounidense dispone de tiempo para analizar los datos antes de decidir cuándo volver a subir las tasas, y señaló que es probable que se produzca un alza más antes de que termine el año.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams, afirmó el martes que el banco central estadounidense dispone de tiempo para analizar los datos antes de decidir cuándo volver a subir las tasas, y señaló que es probable que se produzca un alza más antes de que termine el año. "Con las medidas de política monetaria que adoptamos en nuestra reunión de septiembre, no hay necesidad de actuar con urgencia", afirmó Williams en la Universidad de Buffalo, en Nueva York. Analizar los datos que vayan llegando antes de decidir los próximos pasos "debería aportar mayor claridad" sobre el comportamiento de la economía, señaló Williams. "Si la economía evoluciona de una manera que se ajuste en líneas generales a mi previsión, podría ser adecuado realizar un nuevo ajuste al alza del rango objetivo de los fondos federales a finales de este año para favorecer un retorno más oportuno de la inflación al objetivo", señaló Williams. El funcionario añadió que "ésa es solo mi previsión, y el tiempo —y el conjunto de los datos— lo dirán". Los comentarios de Williams sobre las perspectivas de las tasas se producen en un momento en que los mercados financieros están descontando que la Fed dé continuidad a la subida de tasas de septiembre, que elevó el rango objetivo en un cuarto de punto porcentual a 3,75%-4%. Los mercados de futuros ven muchas posibilidades de que la Fed suba las tasas en su reunión de octubre, una idea a la que Williams pareció oponerse. Williams señaló que, dado el sólido crecimiento de la economía y la estabilidad del mercado laboral, las presiones sobre los precios pueden ser ahora el principal foco de atención de la política monetaria. "Es imperativo que volvamos a situar la inflación en nuestro objetivo del 2% de forma sostenida", afirmó. "Para ello, debemos asegurarnos de que las perturbaciones inflacionarias adversas no se afiancen y de que cualquier efecto de segunda ronda sobre la inflación siga siendo moderado". La Fed está subiendo las tasas para hacer frente a las presiones que llevan más de media década superando el objetivo de inflación del 2%. Dichas presiones se han agravado este año debido a los aranceles comerciales del presidente Donald Trump y al aumento de los precios de la energía vinculado a la guerra en Oriente Medio. A los responsables de la Fed les preocupa cada vez más que la inflación no vuelva al objetivo a tiempo y que sea necesario tomar medidas para garantizar que la población no acabe aceptando como normal una inflación persistentemente alta. Williams señaló que la inversión en inteligencia artificial también está contribuyendo a aumentar las presiones sobre los precios, al tiempo que añadió que las presiones relacionadas con los aranceles se han atenuado en gran medida. Williams afirmó que prevé que la inflación cierre el año en torno al 3,5%, ya que las presiones sobre los precios se moderarán el próximo año, en el camino hacia el retorno de la inflación al objetivo fijado para 2028.

item.title: Red Sox return LHP Garrett Crochet from IL for wild-card round
item.description: The Boston Red Sox reinstated left-hander Garrett Crochet from the 60-day injured list after recovering from left shoulder inflammation as the team gets set to face the rival New York Yankees on Tuesday in an American League wild-card series.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Boston Red Sox reinstated left-hander Garrett Crochet from the 60-day injured list after recovering from left shoulder inflammation as the team gets set to face the rival New York Yankees on Tuesday in an American League wild-card series. Crochet, 27, made just six starts this season and has not pitched in a major league game since April 25 against the Baltimore Orioles. He was 3-3 with a 6.30 ERA to open the first month of the season. A two-time All-Star who finished second in American League Cy Young Award voting last season, Crochet did not make a minor league rehab appearance this season but has thrown bullpen sessions, as well as live batting practice, as part of his recovery. To make room on the 40-man roster, right-hander Justin Slaten was transferred to the 60-day injured list with a right elbow injury. Crochet is expected to be used out of the bullpen by the Red Sox in the current series, although he has not pitched in relief since 2023 when he made 13 appearances for the Chicago White Sox in his return from Tommy John surgery. In six major league seasons, Crochet is 30-27 with a 3.17 ERA in 142 appearances (70 starts) for the White Sox (2020-24) and Red Sox. --Field Level Media

item.title: Athletics' Zack Gelof sues over injury at Detroit's Comerica Park
item.description: Zack Gelof of the Athletics is suing the Detroit Tigers, alleging that a July knee injury was caused by sliding into an exposed metal fence at Comerica Park.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zack Gelof of the Athletics is suing the Detroit Tigers, alleging that a July knee injury was caused by sliding into an exposed metal fence at Comerica Park. Gelof filed the suit Monday in Wayne County (Mich.) Circuit Court. The complaint also names team owner Ilitch Holdings and the Detroit-Wayne County Stadium Authority, which owns the stadium. Gelof, 26, sustained the injury while playing left field in the third inning of a 4-1 loss at Detroit on July 9. While making a sliding catch on a foul ball, he alleges in the lawsuit that his "right knee violently struck an exposed dangerous metal fence on the side wall that protruded into or alongside the playing area." According to a copy of the complaint obtained by the Detroit Free Press, "the collision tore plaintiff Zack Gelof's uniform and caused a deep laceration beneath his right kneecap that narrowly missed the patellar tendon." Gelof did not return to the Athletics' lineup until a month later on Aug. 10. The lawsuit claims the team and ballpark were negligent, noting that padding was installed in the area shortly after the incident. "It doesn't take a stadium design expert to realize that sharp metal fencing in an area where players are required to slide and play around is a recipe for disaster like the one that occurred here," Gelof's attorney Jon Marko said in a statement. "All they had to do was put cheap padding up like they did after Zack was injured and this entire incident could have been avoided. My son's little league diamond is safer." Gelof is seeking unspecified compensation for pain and suffering, economic loss, lost wages, emotional and mental distress, medical bills, attorney fees and other damages. "We are aware of the lawsuit and do not comment on pending litigation," the Tigers said in a statement on Tuesday. Gelof finished the 2026 season batting .256 with 22 home runs, 55 RBIs and 16 stolen bases in 111 games. He started 66 games at third base, 25 in the outfield, 11 at second base and two at designated hitter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Turkey sets up council to oversee investment fund liquidations
item.description: Turkey established a fund coordination council chaired by the vice president to oversee the rapid liquidation of investment funds to protect investor rights following a recent fund crisis, the presidency said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey established a fund coordination council chaired by the vice president to oversee the rapid liquidation of investment funds to protect investor rights following a recent fund crisis, the presidency said on Tuesday. Authorities has launched an audit of recent investment fund transactions in capital markets, the presidency said. The Capital Markets Board presented a roadmap for paying investors, based on the asset and liquidity status of funds under liquidation during a [USN:S8N3YR0AK TEXT:"meeting"] by economy officials and President Tayyip Erdogan. The presidency said the officials discussed additional administrative and legal measures to strengthen capital markets oversight and prevent similar crises recurring. The fund crisis erupted after suspected price manipulation in a number of thinly traded stocks triggered heavy losses and redemption pressures at investment funds. Almost half a million investors hold stakes in more than 100 Turkish investment funds worth [USN:L8N45A04Y TEXT:"$20 billion"] that authorities ordered to be liquidated this month.

item.title: Iranianos sofrem com aumento vertiginoso dos custos de sete meses de guerra
item.description: Os líderes do Irã podem transmitir otimismo em sua guerra contra os Estados Unidos, mas a vida está se tornando cada vez mais difícil para os cidadãos comuns, que não têm condições de arcar com as necessidades básicas ou com o aluguel, à medida que o bloqueio dos EUA corta a principal fonte de renda do Estado — as exportações de petróleo.
item.dc:creator: John Davison, Emily Giles
item.content:encoded: Os líderes do Irã podem transmitir otimismo em sua guerra contra os Estados Unidos, mas a vida está se tornando cada vez mais difícil para os cidadãos comuns, que não têm condições de arcar com as necessidades básicas ou com o aluguel, à medida que o bloqueio dos EUA corta a principal fonte de renda do Estado — as exportações de petróleo. De um engenheiro forçado a deixar Teerã devido ao alto aluguel a uma mulher obrigada a parar de fumar por causa do preço dos cigarros e cuidadores que lutam para comprar remédios, todas as áreas da vida cotidiana são afetadas. “Sou obrigado a vender meus produtos com um lucro muito pequeno e insignificante, mas não posso fechar meu negócio porque, se o fizer, ficarei desempregado”, disse Behnam Riazi, dono de um restaurante entrevistado diante das câmeras em Teerã. Riazi não pode aumentar seus preços porque seus clientes não podem pagar mais — e a maioria, de qualquer forma, compra apenas o essencial agora. Não está claro até que ponto as tensões econômicas podem levar o Irã a um acordo diplomático, já que o país reforça seu próprio controle sobre as exportações de energia do Golfo pelo Estreito de Ormuz, elevando os preços do petróleo e do gás nos EUA e em todo o mundo. MISÉRIA ECONÔMICA PODE IMPULSIONAR A DIPLOMACIA No entanto, a mais recente onda de diplomacia foi parcialmente impulsionada pelas tensões econômicas, segundo fontes dos EUA, do Oriente Médio e do Irã na semana passada. Autoridades iranianas têm expressado repetidamente temores de agitação social e reprimido impiedosamente qualquer sinal de dissidência. Em janeiro, mais de um mês antes de os EUA e Israel iniciarem sua guerra contra o Irã, as autoridades mataram milhares de manifestantes exasperados por anos de sofrimento econômico acumulado. Mas agora, todos com quem a Reuters conversou disseram ter preocupações diárias demais para pensar em protestar. Hediyeh, uma dona de casa na casa dos 60 anos no norte do Irã, sobrevive com a aposentadoria do marido, que era funcionário público. Ela mal consegue pagar pelos remédios ou mesmo pelas fraldas para adultos de que sua mãe idosa, que tem Alzheimer, precisa. Ela queria comprar uma mochila nova para o neto no primeiro dia de aula neste outono, mas o preço era cinco ou seis vezes maior do que ela esperava e, no fim, só conseguiu comprar um caderno e lápis para ele. Como a maioria dos iranianos entrevistados pela Reuters por telefone ou por aplicativo de mensagens, ela não quis se identificar, temendo punição por falar com a mídia estrangeira. A.J., um professor que pediu para ser identificado apenas pelas iniciais, também disse que nem sempre consegue pagar pelos remédios de que sua mãe precisa. Ele já se mudou para morar com a mãe e os irmãos em um vilarejo no norte do país, deixando Teerã depois que as aulas passaram a ser ministradas online por causa da guerra, mas teme não ter mais condições financeiras de voltar caso as aulas presenciais sejam retomadas. Em Sanandaj, capital da província do Curdistão, a psicoterapeuta Nazanin, de 34 anos, desistiu de fumar por causa do custo, depois de anteriormente ter achado impossível fazê-lo, disse ela. Aqueles que têm condições de contornar as formas habituais de obter bens ou serviços por meio do mercado negro estão percebendo que ele se tornou mais difundido, embora o custo tenha aumentado. Um homem disse ter pago US$200 em moeda forte a um cirurgião para contornar o processo burocrático necessário para uma operação. Outro disse que os pedidos de suborno por parte da polícia estavam se tornando mais frequentes e que teve de pagar mais do que antes depois de ser parado em um posto de controle sem documentos de identificação. CORTES DE PESSOAL NO SETOR PRIVADO Um arquiteto, que se identificou apenas pelas iniciais A.A., disse que até mesmo os iranianos mais ricos estavam cortando gastos: “Todos eles ficaram pobres em comparação com o estilo de vida que costumavam ter.” Um pneu furou na semana passada e ele está tendo que dirigir com o pneu sobressalente durante as duas semanas que levará para conseguir um pneu de reposição barato; ele não tem mais condições de comprar aqueles disponíveis imediatamente. Ele teme que o Irã esteja caminhando para uma escassez de combustível, o que poderia interromper as cadeias de abastecimento e causar um caos econômico ainda maior. A guerra já está causando pesadas perdas de empregos em todo o setor privado. M.H., uma mulher em Teerã que também pediu para ser identificada apenas pelas iniciais, disse que perdeu o emprego este mês no departamento de compras de uma empresa local, embora seu contrato de um ano tivesse sido renovado apenas no dia anterior. Agora ela precisa devolver o dinheiro que a empresa havia depositado no sistema de previdência social do Irã para o próximo ano. Sua família estabeleceu prioridades rígidas nos gastos, com a alimentação em primeiro lugar. “Ainda bem que ainda podemos pagar pela internet, assim podemos ficar conectados online, talvez assistir a um filme”, disse ela. Bijan, de 40 anos, um ex-engenheiro que agora dá aulas particulares para ganhar dinheiro, disse que ele e a esposa deixaram o apartamento em Teerã e se mudaram para uma área que ele descreveu como “meia favela” nos arredores da capital. O casal esgotou suas economias e planeja se mudar para outra cidade, onde esperam viver com menos gastos. Os donos de lojas percebem a queda no padrão de vida melhor do que a maioria das pessoas. Ramin Yousefnia disse, em uma entrevista filmada em Teerã, que todos os clientes de seu supermercado reduziram os gastos. “Algo que costumavam comprar em quantidades de cinco ou dez, agora só conseguem comprar dois”, disse ele. “Nem me faça falar sobre poupança. Essa é a realidade.”

item.title: Departamento de Justicia de EEUU acusa a un venezolano baleado por un agente del ICE en Austin
item.description: Un venezolano baleado por un agente federal de inmigración el 20 de septiembre en Austin, Texas, compareció el martes ante un tribunal federal tras ser acusado de agredir, resistirse, interferir y obstaculizar a un funcionario federal, informó el Departamento de Justicia.
item.dc:creator: Julia Harte
item.content:encoded: Un venezolano [USN:L6N45E0PF TEXT:"baleado por un agente federal de inmigración"] el 20 de septiembre en Austin, Texas, compareció el martes ante un tribunal federal tras ser acusado de agredir, resistirse, interferir y obstaculizar a un funcionario federal, informó el Departamento de Justicia. La denuncia contra Wilber Rafael Garces Pérez, de 28 años, que cita imágenes de la cámara que llevaba uno de los agentes del ICE que lo detuvieron ese día, afirma que cuando le pidieron que saliera de su coche, arrancó y golpeó a un agente en el torso con el espejo retrovisor. El video no se ha hecho público. Según la denuncia, presentada el lunes ante el Tribunal de Distrito para el Distrito Oeste de Texas, el agente, que no llevaba cámara, persiguió a Garces Pérez en su coche y pronto lo alcanzó. En ese momento, Garces Pérez intentó atropellar al agente, quien le disparó con su pistola, según la denuncia. Los videos del incidente disponibles públicamente no muestran el tiroteo, pero sí muestran a Garces Pérez herido en el auto después. Según la denuncia, Garces Pérez le dijo al funcionario del DHS que investigaba el caso que le dispararon después de que un agente estrellara su camioneta contra su auto, haciéndolo girar. El abogado de Garces Pérez no respondió de inmediato a la solicitud de comentarios. Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch publicó en Instagram el domingo que su cliente aún tiene la bala alojada en el cuerpo y una clavícula fracturada, y que [USN:L6N45G13E TEXT:"sus allegados"] están preocupados de que pueda sufrir sepsis y daños permanentes si no se somete a cirugía pronto. El Departamento de Seguridad Nacional ha declarado que está recibiendo la atención médica adecuada. Si bien el Gobierno de Estados Unidos ha presentado cargos penales contra al menos 851 personas por atacar o entorpecer la labor de agentes federales, una [USN:L6N43V0Z5 TEXT:"revisión de los registros de los tribunales realizada por Reuters"] en julio reveló que el 31% de los casos concluidos habían sido desestimados, frente a una tasa de desestimación del 8% de todos los casos penales federales. Garces Pérez tiene previsto comparecer el miércoles ante un juez federal de inmigración en Texas para una audiencia en la que se determinará si puede permanecer en el país.

item.title: EUA aprovam construção de 1º reator nuclear modular de pequeno porte do país
item.description: A Comissão Reguladora Nuclear dos EUA (NRC) aprovou uma licença de construção para a Tennessee Valley Authority construir o primeiro reator modular pequeno comercial do país, informou a agência nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Comissão Reguladora Nuclear dos EUA (NRC) aprovou uma licença de construção para a Tennessee Valley Authority (TVC.N) construir o primeiro reator modular pequeno comercial do país, informou a agência nesta terça-feira. “A TVA planeja construir um reator de água fervente da GE Vernova Hitachi de 300 megawatts para ajudar a atender à crescente demanda regional por energia”, afirmou a agência em comunicado. Os reatores de água fervente utilizam o calor da fissão nuclear para ferver a água dentro do vaso do reator, produzindo vapor que aciona diretamente uma turbina para gerar eletricidade. O projeto recebeu licença de construção após a NRC concluir uma análise de 14 meses, marcando a segunda grande aprovação de reator pela agência neste ano, informou a agência. A TVA precisará de uma licença de operação separada da NRC antes de carregar o combustível e iniciar as operações, informou a agência. A TVA já havia recebido uma licença preliminar para o local da usina em 2019. (Por Noel John)

item.title: Anthropic’s $2 trln goal is AI’s biggest moonshot
item.description: The Claude maker posted big growth and a 40% gross margin last year, but also an $8 bln operating loss. Its 2026 figures will groan further under huge spending promises to feed demand. Even next to recently launched frenemy SpaceX, CEO Dario Amodei’s valuation target looks steep.
item.dc:creator: Karen Kwok
item.content:encoded: Anthropic hopes to ramp up a season for gargantuan public debuts started by SpaceX (SPCX.O) . In doing so, the artificial intelligence lab behind Claude will push investors to accept yet wilder financial ambitions. Key details from the company’s IPO prospectus offer a glimpse at tantalizingly massive growth to support a $2 trillion valuation target, as [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"reported"] by Reuters. They also make even Elon Musk’s rockets-to-robots concern look down to Earth. According to documents reviewed by Reuters, Anthropic's revenue rose nearly 12-fold in 2025, to $4.6 billion. Its implied gross margin, or revenue less costs mostly comprised of computing responses to user queries, swung to roughly 40% last year, from negative 95%, an extraordinary turnaround. The hope is that continued rapid growth can further pay off boss Dario Amodei’s massive investments in computing power. While full details of this year’s results are yet to emerge, take the company’s $16 billion in [USN:L6N41Y0ZA TEXT:"revenue"] in the first and second quarters, and assume it holds steady. That should lead to just shy of $40 billion in sales for all of 2026, before accounting for any further spurts. At a $2 trillion valuation, less $120 billion of net cash as reported by The Information, Anthropic would be worth roughly 47 times that revenue. That would exceed SpaceX's already sky-high multiple of about 42 times expected sales this year, based on Visible Alpha data. Moreover, 83% of Anthropic’s 2025 revenue was from metered consumption, up from 75% in 2024. Such customers can cut usage quickly if budgets tighten or cheaper, alternative models emerge. And although last year’s figures miss much of the boost from the “vibe coding” phenomenon sparked by Claude Code, recent innovations by rival Meta Platforms (META.O) in offering AI agents for ordinary tasks may push growth into the consumer end of the market, where Anthropic has a weaker hand. Then there’s the continued, massive spending on data centers to train models. Anthropic spent over $7 billion on computing infrastructure in 2025, or $1.60 for every dollar of revenue. Granted, it spent $6.53 per dollar of revenue in 2024, but last year still saw an $8 billion operating loss. Anthropic also points to over $500 billion in spending commitments spread across multi-year contracts. Big chunks of that sum, agreed to with Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Google, Amazon.com (AMZN.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) , cannot just be walked away from. A more flexible arrangement with SpaceX came at [USN:L6N42414K TEXT:"heavy cost"]. To boot, these are both partners and rivals, who might reprioritize in-house AI efforts. Amodei can point to faster growth than even Musk’s company, but has no ballast like a quasi-monopolistic rocket empire. If Anthropic’s growth continues to largely enrich its frenemies, the company’s own valuation ambitions will begin to look starry-eyed. Follow Karen Kwok on LinkedIn and X . Artificial intelligence lab Anthropic's revenue grew 12-fold in 2025 to nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, according to details of an IPO prospectus reported by Reuters. Anthropic reported a net loss of $42 billion in 2025, and plans to spend $518 billion on cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years, according to the documents. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: 英中銀の利上げ根拠「乏しい」、エネ高のインフレ波及見極めへ＝テイラー委員
item.description: [ロンドン ２９日 ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）のテイラー金融政策委員は２９日、エネルギー価格の高騰...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英中銀の利上げ根拠「乏しい」、エネ高のインフレ波及見極めへ＝テイラー委員 3:35 配信

写真は英中銀ビル。１６日撮影。REUTERS/Corey Rudy

[ロンドン　２９日　ロイター] - イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）のテイラー金融政策委員は２９日、エネルギー価格の高騰が幅広い経済分野へのインフレ波及として明確に表れない限り、利上げの根拠は乏しいままだとの見解を示した。

テイラー氏は英国立経済社会研究所の講演で、「エネルギー価格が長期間にわたって高止まりし、より広範なインフレの持続性への波及を示すより明確なシグナルが生じない限り、さらなる利上げの根拠は私にとって説得力を持たない」と述べた。

現在の見通しについて、ロシアのウクライナ全面侵攻によって原油価格が急騰し、コロナ禍後の労働市場の逼迫に拍車をかけ、インフレを２桁台に押し上げた２０２２年の状況とは類似していないと指摘。

「これほど目に見えるエネルギーショックの後、多くのエネルギー集約型の財（モノ）・サービス分野におけるインフレは、予想されたほど加速していない」と述べた。

テイラー氏はまた、追加利上げがあるとの根拠のない市場観測をあおることなく、英中銀がインフレ抑制のために１回だけ利上げを行うことが現実的かどうかは不明だとの見方も示した。

テイラー氏はさらに、２０２７年の企業の賃金見通しに関する英中銀の年次調査が、利上げの是非を判断する上で鍵になるとの認識を示した。「来年１月に公表予定の２７年の賃金見通しに関する調査は、非常に重要なデータポイントとなる」と述べた。

また、英中銀の１２月会合の時点で入手可能な暫定結果にも注目すると説明。前回調査の水準である３％をやや上回る程度、あるいはそれ以下の数値であれば、インフレ圧力が抑制されているとの安心材料になると述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：英新財務相、実務手腕に一定評価も支出拡大・増税不安消えず アングル：英国経済、ＥＵ離脱から10年の軌跡 アングル：ブレグジット10年、英ＥＵの溝なお深く　極右台頭も重し 焦点：ＥＵ離脱から10年、苦闘続く英輸出企業　非離脱シナリオより低成長の予測 最終更新: 9/30(水) 3:35 ロイター

item.title: At UN, developing nations call for bigger say in shaping AI future
item.description: Developing nations are demanding a greater role in shaping the rules governing artificial intelligence, warning that a technology poised to transform economies could instead deepen global inequalities if its development and regulation remain concentrated in wealthy countries.
item.dc:creator: Doyinsola Oladipo
item.content:encoded: Developing nations are demanding a greater role in shaping the rules governing artificial intelligence, warning that a technology poised to transform economies could instead deepen global inequalities if its development and regulation remain concentrated in wealthy countries. The debate at last week's UN festival of diplomacy in New York highlighted [USN:FWN4560E8 TEXT:"mounting concern"] among leaders from Africa, Asia and Latin America around the increasingly powerful technology after several safety breaches, and as top researchers have warned it could destroy humanity. "Developing countries cannot be reduced to the role of mere users of technologies designed elsewhere, nor should be the mere recipients of standards and norms that they did not adequately participate in shaping," said Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. "We must ensure that technological transformations of the 21st century do not reproduce the economic imbalances of previous decades," Wagner said. She made the remarks at a Security Council session [USN:L6N45E0VV TEXT:"dedicated to AI"] that featured top executives of leading labs, including Sam Altman from OpenAI and Dario Amodei from Anthropic, who urged governments to work together to manage the technology. Underscoring the surge in interest in the subject, Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh, who chaired the UN debate this year, said that, "four years ago, AI was raised in this hall by only five delegations – this year, 128 delegations addressed it." 'A QUESTION OF GOVERNANCE' "Many framed AI as a question of governance: Who designs it, who benefits? Who bears the risks, and who is accountable when harm occurs," added the Bangladeshi foreign minister as he concluded the marathon of speeches at the UN. AI could enable developing countries to gain a century's worth of development in a decade if they act quickly on power, connectivity and skills gaps, the World Bank [USN:L8N4401YH TEXT:"said in a report last month"]. The International Monetary Fund said in July that AI [USN:L6N43M0EG TEXT:"could boost"] Sub-Saharan Africa's economy by about 4% over the next decade under the right circumstances. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres compared debates around AI risks and climate change and said that developing nations should have an equal voice in both. "The climate crisis went from distant warning to daily reality and artificial intelligence moved at a speed that has blindsided even those who created it," he said. "These are not separate crises. They are chapters of the same story, the story of power: Who has it. Who is denied it. How it is used. And how it is changing," Guterres told the UN. As with climate change, Guterres and Global South leaders urged a coordinated global action rather than isolated national responses to AI threats. Their focus on regulation stood in sharp contrast with remarks by US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed AI risks as a "hoax" and "sick conspiracy" and told the UN that – like climate change – they were vastly overblown. “The very same people who said we'll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming – a name since reborn to climate change because the planet was cooling, not warming, and nobody was dead – these are the same people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us all," Trump said. Belize Prime Minister John Briceño said AI, if well governed, could widen access to knowledge and improve public services. But he also warned: "Poorly governed, it can deepen inequality, expose critical systems, displace workers and leave developing countries dependent on technologies and rules designed elsewhere.”

item.title: Ken Paxton's 2022 remarks on Uvalde school shooting clipped to omit context
item.description: Audio from a 2022 interview with US Senate candidate Ken Paxton, a Texas Republican, is edited to omit the context of his full remarks about the Uvalde school shooting and misleadingly shared online as “newly uncovered.”
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Audio from a 2022 interview with US Senate candidate Ken Paxton, a Texas Republican, is edited to omit the context of his full remarks about the Uvalde school shooting and misleadingly shared online as “newly uncovered.” Paxton, who is running in a [USN:L6N44T0XY TEXT:"tight race"] against Democrat James Talarico, was the Texas attorney general on May 24, 2022, when an 18-year-old gunman [USN:S0N2XF01A TEXT:"killed 19 students"] and two teachers at Texas’ Robb Elementary School before being [USN:L1N3YN02M TEXT:"shot dead"] by law enforcement. Paxton addressed the shooting in the second segment of the May 29, 2022, Smart Talk with Trey Graham podcast . An excerpt from that podcast appears in a September 23 X post captioned, “NEWLY UNCOVERED AUDIO: Texas GOP US Senate candidate Ken Paxton calls the Uvalde shooting a ‘plan’ by ‘God’ and says ‘life is short’ about children murdered in an elementary school. This man is vile.” The audio clip in the post includes Paxton saying, “Look, there's always a plan. I believe God always has a plan. Life is short no matter what it is.” However, in the podcast, Graham, a North Texas pastor, asked Paxton to share any words of comfort or encouragement to the families who lost their children in the shooting. Paxton, who opposes gun control , said, “It's difficult to give comfort. If I, if I lost one of my children, I'd be pretty devastated, especially in a, in a way that is so senseless and, you know, seemingly has no purpose. I, I think I would, I would just have to, if, if, if I had the opportunity to talk to people, I'd have to say, ‘Look, there's always a plan. I believe God always has a plan. Life is short no matter what it is, and certainly, we, we're not gonna make sense of, you know, a young child being shot, and killed way before their life expectancy. And so even though we can't make sense of it, I would just have to encourage them to hold onto their faith and to hold onto their belief that there really is purpose in, in what God does. And we may not know it now, but someday we will.” The owner of the X account that posted the excerpt told Reuters by email that Paxton’s remarks were “widely reported on at the time” as insensitive and shared links to articles describing the backlash. She did not respond to questions about the source of the short clip, which her post describes as “newly uncovered audio.” A spokesperson for Graham declined to comment but also referred Reuters to a 2022 opinion piece in the Washington Post titled, “Texas AG Paxton’s shameful Uvalde cop-out: ‘God always has a plan'.” Paxton’s office and campaign did not immediately respond to requests for comment. VERDICT Missing context. An audio excerpt of 2022 remarks by Ken Paxton about the Uvalde school shooting is not “newly uncovered” and omits the full context of his response to a podcaster’s question. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

item.title: ANP avança para reduzir concentração no mercado de gás apesar de resistência da Petrobras
item.description: A Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) deu mais um passo em direção à implementação do programa de "gas release", iniciativa do governo que visa reduzir a concentração do mercado brasileiro de gás natural e a predominância da Petrobras no setor, indicaram discussões sobre o tema nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Viga Gaier, Marta Nogueira
item.content:encoded: A Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) deu mais um passo em direção à implementação do programa de "gas release", iniciativa do governo que visa reduzir a concentração do mercado brasileiro de gás natural e a predominância da Petrobras no setor, indicaram discussões sobre o tema nesta terça-feira. Na véspera, a ANP encerrou uma consulta pública sobre a proposta, apesar de resistência da estatal, que voltou a pedir um adiamento das discussões nesta terça-feira. O programa do "gas release" prevê a realização de leilões regulados pela autarquia para oferta de volumes de gás hoje adquiridos pela Petrobras de terceiros produtores ou importados da Bolívia, permitindo que outros comercializadores tenham acesso a esses volumes e concorram com a estatal na venda do combustível. Durante workshop promovido pela reguladora nesta terça-feira, representantes do governo, da ANP e da indústria reforçaram o apoio à iniciativa, prevista na Lei do Gás, argumentando que a abertura do mercado ocorrida nos últimos anos ainda não foi suficiente para eliminar a elevada concentração na oferta do combustível. Segundo estudo apresentado pela ANP, a Petrobras ainda detém participação média de 59% no mercado atacadista não termelétrico atendido pela malha integrada de transporte. Também presente no evento, o gerente-executivo de gás e energia da Petrobras, Álvaro Tupiassú, reiterou que a companhia não vê necessidade de implementar o "gas release" neste momento, argumentando que a participação da estatal no mercado já vem caindo nos últimos anos. Tupiassú defendeu ainda um pedido de adiamento da audiência pública sobre o tema, prevista atualmente para 21 de outubro. A audiência é o último passo antes que a agência decida sobre o formato definitivo do programa. "Achamos que essa discussão tem que levar mais tempo e que é possível levar mais tempo sem comprometer o eventual objetivo de fazer vigência (do programa) em 2028", afirmou Tupiassú, durante participação no workshop. Durante o congresso ROG.e, na semana passada, a presidente da Petrobras, Magda Chambriard, defendeu a atuação da companhia como compradora de gás de terceiros, afirmando que esse tipo de arranjo ajuda a viabilizar investimentos e é comum em outros mercados. O diretor da autarquia, Pietro Mendes, entretanto, rebateu os pedidos de adiamento da Petrobras e afirmou que "cabe à ANP pensar no todo... não para maximizar o interesse do monopolista, mas sim para maximizar o interesse da sociedade brasileira". O diretor acrescentou que a agência "não pode se conformar com o preço do gás natural que temos no Brasil". "A gente já analisou o pedido de adiamento e já houve um julgamento pela diretoria colegiada, por unanimidade, de não adiar a audiência pública", afirmou, ponderando que até poderia avaliar novo pedido, mas que os fundamentos não são oportunos. Pietro também criticou os argumentos usados para defender uma postergação das discussões. "A gente não pode aceitar prorrogação por argumentos maniqueístas, do bem e do mal. 'A agência má que está colocando em discussão o gas release, a agência está adotando uma medida que é absurda por si só', sem que a gente tenha um espaço para debate", disse. Segundo ele, a ANP precisa ter sua competência técnica respeitada e não pode ser impedida de discutir medidas previstas na legislação para aumentar a concorrência no mercado de gás. O secretário de Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis do Ministério de Minas e Energia, Renato Dutra, afirmou que o programa está alinhado à política energética do governo e faz parte de uma agenda mais ampla voltada ao aumento da oferta e à redução dos preços do gás para a indústria brasileira. A iniciativa integra o programa Gás para Empregar, lançado pelo governo Lula com o objetivo de ampliar a oferta de gás natural e reduzir custos para consumidores industriais.

item.title: Five things to know about the college sports bill that passed the US Senate
item.description: The US Senate passed legislation this week to regulate college sports, a multibillion-dollar industry that has been upended in recent years by increased earning opportunities for student athletes.
item.dc:creator: Nolan Mccaskill
item.content:encoded: The US Senate passed legislation this week to regulate college sports, a multibillion-dollar industry that has been upended in recent years by increased earning opportunities for student athletes. Here are five things to know about the bill's passage: WHAT JUST HAPPENED? The Senate voted 77-22 on Monday evening to pass the proposal, which now heads to the US House of Representatives. HOW WOULD IT CHANGE COLLEGE SPORTS? The proposal would create national standards around student athlete transfers, eligibility and compensation for name, image and likeness use. It would permit one school transfer "without losing or delaying eligibility to participate." A student athlete who transferred institutions a second time would be ineligible for one year aside from four exceptions including the departure of a head coach, sexual assault or harassment and the discontinuation of a sport. Student athletes would also be limited to five years of eligibility with exceptions for pregnancy, religious missions, active-duty military service and a "serious athletic injury or medical condition." The measure would protect student athletes' rights to NIL compensation and require disclosure of NIL deals that exceed $600. IS IT CONTROVERSIAL? The legislation includes several controversial components. For example, its national standards on transfers, eligibility and name, image and likeness deals would preempt state laws. More than 30 states have already enacted their own name, image and likeness laws. The bill sidesteps one of college sports' biggest legal battles: whether the athletes should be classified as employees rather than students participating in extracurricular activities. The proposal allows athletes to sue to enforce its provisions, rather than requiring arbitration, though critics say lawsuits are burdensome to individuals. "Student-athletes often have limited time, resources, and legal expertise," Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester, a Delaware Democrat, said in a statement. "They should not bear primary responsibility for identifying violations and suing their schools or athletic programs to secure the protections provided by the bill." Blunt Rochester also warned that Congress should not lock in terms "that could limit student-athletes' ability to negotiate or collectively bargain over them in the future." WHO VOTED FOR IT? Fifty of the chamber's 53 Republicans supported the legislation. Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska did not vote. Senators Rick Scott of Florida and Rand Paul of Kentucky opposed it. Paul proposed an amendment that would have gutted the bill. Paul's amendment was overwhelmingly rejected, failing 1-94 with only Paul voting in favor of it. Twenty-seven members of the Democratic Caucus backed the legislation. Opponents said the measure could limit athletes' leverage in future labor and antitrust disputes, even as it created new health, safety and compensation protections. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? The measure now moves to the House, which has recessed until after November 3's midterm elections. A majority of the 433-member House — two seats are vacant — would have to approve the bill to send it to President Donald Trump's desk to be signed into law.

The legislation includes several controversial components. For example, its national standards on transfers, eligibility and name, image and likeness deals would preempt state laws. More than 30 states have already enacted their own name, image and likeness laws. The bill sidesteps one of college sports' biggest legal battles: whether the athletes should be classified as employees rather than students participating in extracurricular activities. The proposal allows athletes to sue to enforce its provisions, rather than requiring arbitration, though critics say lawsuits are burdensome to individuals. "Student-athletes often have limited time, resources, and legal expertise," Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester, a Delaware Democrat, said in a statement. "They should not bear primary responsibility for identifying violations and suing their schools or athletic programs to secure the protections provided by the bill."  Blunt Rochester also warned that Congress should not lock in terms "that could limit student-athletes' ability to negotiate or collectively bargain over them in the future." WHO VOTED FOR IT? Fifty of the chamber's 53 Republicans supported the legislation. Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska did not vote. Senators Rick Scott of Florida and Rand Paul of Kentucky opposed it. Paul proposed an amendment that would have gutted the bill. Paul's amendment was overwhelmingly rejected, failing 1-94 with only Paul voting in favor of it. Twenty-seven members of the Democratic Caucus backed the legislation.  Opponents said the measure could limit athletes' leverage in future labor and antitrust disputes, even as it created new health, safety and compensation protections. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? The measure now moves to the House, which has recessed until after November 3's midterm elections. A majority of the 433-member House — two seats are vacant — would have to approve the bill to send it to President Donald Trump's desk to be signed into law.

Source: Reuters
