item.title: Trump government ads draw artist protest, regulatory complaints
item.description: Taxpayer-funded television ads featuring President Donald Trump drew fresh scrutiny on Tuesday after the recording artist behind a song used in one spot demanded the White House stop using his music and a watchdog group asked federal regulators to pull the commercials from the air.
item.dc:creator: Dawn Kopecki, Helen Coster
item.content:encoded: Taxpayer-funded television ads featuring President Donald Trump drew fresh scrutiny on Tuesday after the recording artist behind a song used in one spot demanded the White House stop using his music and a watchdog group asked federal regulators to pull the commercials from the air. The developments added to growing criticism of the three nationally broadcast ads, which celebrate a "golden age of America" and are airing five weeks before midterm elections, with ethics experts and lawmakers from both parties questioning whether public funds are being used to promote Trump politically. Attorneys for Christian Berishaj, who performs as JMSN, sent the White House a cease-and-desist letter saying his song "Love Me" was used without permission, while Public Citizen filed complaints with regulators arguing the spots are campaign advertisements that should not be produced or distributed with taxpayer resources. Democratic Senators Patty Murray and Chris Murphy asked Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Tuesday to answer for the ads, saying the administration had diverted $20 million from the agency for the ad campaign. "This administration’s defense of using Americans’ tax dollars to air these ads is as absurd as it is offensive," they wrote in a letter to Mullin. The White House did not immediately respond to Reuters questions on Tuesday about the cost of the ads or criticism that they amount to political advertising funded by taxpayers. It previously defended the spots as "public service announcements" intended to promote patriotism rather than campaign ads. The ads end with the disclaimer "Paid for by the US Government." 'LOVE ME,' THE ADS IMPLORE One ad features Trump declaring that "America will never be a communist country" while a chorus repeats the words "love me." Another combines images of Mount Rushmore with footage of Trump praising a "golden age of America." A third describes a "final battle" against the "deep state" and closely resembles one of Trump's 2024 campaign advertisements. Berishaj said in an Instagram post that he would "never authorize my music to be used for ANY political agenda or campaign." Public Citizen asked broadcasters to stop airing the spots and urged federal authorities to investigate whether executive branch officials improperly engaged in partisan political activity. "These ads are campaign advertisements, which should be produced and distributed on campaign time and without involving taxpayer dollars," the group said. Critics say the spots may violate longstanding restrictions on government propaganda and political activity.

item.title: OpenAI desafia Meta com agente Dots, que funciona ininterruptamente, em sua iniciativa de IA empresarial
item.description: A OpenAI apresentou nesta terça-feira agentes sempre ativos chamados Dots, que perseguem objetivos do usuário em diversos aplicativos de forma autônoma, intensificando sua investida no lucrativo mercado corporativo e competindo diretamente com a Meta na corrida para vender IA que possa funcionar de forma autônoma.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A OpenAI apresentou nesta terça-feira agentes sempre ativos chamados Dots, que perseguem objetivos do usuário em diversos aplicativos de forma autônoma, intensificando sua investida no lucrativo mercado corporativo e competindo diretamente com a Meta (META.O) na corrida para vender IA que possa funcionar de forma autônoma. Os agentes da Dots visam capitalizar a crescente demanda por agentes capazes de lidar com tarefas cotidianas com pouca supervisão. O interesse por essas ferramentas aumentou consideravelmente desde que o Muse, da Meta, atraiu milhões de downloads no início deste mês e impulsionou as ações de empresas que, segundo investidores, podem se beneficiar ou ser impactadas por serviços autônomos de IA. A OpenAI lançou o agente em seu evento anual para desenvolvedores em San Francisco nesta terça-feira, aproveitando também para destacar sua crescente presença no mercado corporativo e junto aos consumidores, um sinal de que a boa aceitação do modelo Astra permitiu que a empresa recuperasse terreno na corrida da IA. A notícia surge um dia depois de a OpenAI ter suspendido o lançamento de um modelo Astra mais poderoso, alegando que este demonstrava uma alta disposição para enganar os usuários sobre suas ações. A empresa está sob escrutínio depois de seus agentes de IA terem invadido os serviços da Hugging Face e de um website de saúde do governo australiano durante testes internos. Crescer rapidamente é crucial para os planos da OpenAI de investir dezenas de bilhões de dólares em data centers de IA e acompanhar rivais como a Anthropic e a Meta. A empresa, que impulsionou o boom da IA com o ChatGPT no final de 2022, também está se preparando para um IPO que pode avaliá-la em mais de US$1 trilhão. A rival Anthropic pode valer US$2 trilhões quando abrir seu capital. GERENCIANDO PROJETOS EM EVOLUÇÃO Os Dots utilizam o modelo avançado GPT-6 Astra da OpenAI e conseguem gerenciar projetos à medida que evoluem, como atualizar uma proposta de vendas quando as necessidades do cliente mudam e criar uma demonstração funcional para revisão. Os usuários podem se comunicar com os Dots no Slack e no Teams, e os agentes podem utilizar as ferramentas Codex e ChatGPT Work da OpenAI para pesquisar, analisar dados, preparar documentos e desenvolver software. Na terça-feira, a OpenAI destacou as medidas de segurança incorporadas ao Dots. Afirmou que os usuários podem definir regras personalizadas que determinam o que o Dots pode fazer e quando os agentes devem solicitar permissão, acrescentando que tarefas sensíveis, como alterar senhas e excluir dados permanentemente, exigem o consentimento explícito do usuário. A empresa também afirmou que os Dots funcionam em seus próprios computadores em nuvem e que estava implementando ferramentas de inteligência privada para verificar riscos de segurança sem reter os dados de clientes corporativos. Vários executivos de tecnologia, incluindo Alex Karp, presidente-executivo da Palantir (PLTR.O) , afirmaram nos últimos meses que as companhias precisam ter certeza de que as empresas de IA não estão retendo seus dados, especialmente em setores regulamentados como saúde e finanças. A Reuters informou na sexta-feira que a OpenAI ainda estava trabalhando para entender a extensão total da atividade de seus agentes desonestos, dois meses após o ataque à Hugging Face, sendo o exemplo mais recente o vazamento de 53 imagens de usuários do ChatGPT, segundo a própria startup. A OpenAI reiterou na terça-feira que não utiliza, por padrão, os dados de seus clientes corporativos para treinar sua IA e que os usuários do plano pessoal podem optar por não compartilhar conversas e trabalhos do Dots usados para treinamento. O número de usuários semanais do Codex e do ChatGPT Work ultrapassou 35 milhões, um aumento significativo em relação aos cerca de 5 milhões de usuários do Codex em junho, informou a empresa nesta terça-feira. Já o ChatGPT, voltado para o consumidor, agora conta com mais de 1,2 bilhão de usuários semanais. A empresa está lançando uma série de novas ofertas, incluindo um espaço de trabalho compartilhado para equipes de negócios e IA chamado ChatGPT Space, o modelo GPT-6.1 Sol mais acessível e um plano Pro de US$500 que oferece maior uso e desempenho mais rápido. (Por Deepa Seetharaman e Aditya Soni)

item.title: BP proposes six-year labor contract at Whiting refinery
item.description: BP said on Tuesday it is proposing a six-year labor contract for workers at its 440,000-barrel-per-day Whiting refinery in Indiana as negotiations with United Steelworkers (USW) Local 7-1 continue.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: BP (BP.L) said on Tuesday it is proposing a six-year labor contract for workers at its 440,000-barrel-per-day Whiting refinery in Indiana as negotiations with United Steelworkers (USW) Local 7-1 continue. The company said the six-year term would provide stability for the refinery and employees. "6-year term would give you certainty in your pay, your benefits, and your working conditions for years," BP said. The final two years of the proposed agreement would match future National Oil Bargaining Program (NOBP) pattern wage-rate increases. BP is also proposing a longer notice period before the union can strike or the company can initiate a lockout. The company said it would continue talks with USW 7-1 representatives. BP [USN:L6N42Y162 TEXT:"locked out"] its workers at the Whiting refinery in March in a dispute with the union over its next contract.

item.title: OpenAI targets $30 billion funding at $1.4 trillion valuation, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: OpenAI aims to raise at least $30 billion in a funding round and is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, not including the money raised, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OpenAI aims to raise at least $30 billion in a funding round and is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, not including the money raised, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter. Here are more details: The fundraising discussions are at an early stage and terms could change, Bloomberg reported, adding that the demand for the round is being led by investors. The proposed round would serve as a bridge financing to provide capital in place of an IPO, the report said. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The company had closed a funding round in March with $122 billion in committed capital, valuing it at $852 billion. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said [USN:L6N45500D TEXT:"earlier this month"] that the company would not go public in 2026, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence. OpenAI's [USN:L4N45L1EC TEXT:"annualized revenue run rate"] is nearing $70 billion, having risen more than 70% since the beginning of the third quarter, Reuters reported earlier on Tuesday.

item.title: EUA impõem sanções a 10 pessoas e entidades por suposta aquisição de armas para o Irã
item.description: Os Estados Unidos impuseram sanções a 10 pessoas físicas e jurídicas, incluindo algumas sediadas na China, em Hong Kong e no Paquistão, por ajudarem o Ministério da Defesa do Irã a adquirir armas e componentes, informou o Departamento do Tesouro dos EUA nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os Estados Unidos impuseram sanções a 10 pessoas físicas e jurídicas, incluindo algumas sediadas na China, em Hong Kong e no Paquistão, por ajudarem o Ministério da Defesa do Irã a adquirir armas e componentes, informou o Departamento do Tesouro dos EUA nesta terça-feira. As sanções fazem parte de uma iniciativa mais ampla do governo Trump para isolar economicamente o Irã e forçá-lo a negociar o fim da guerra entre os EUA e o Irã, que começou em fevereiro. “No âmbito da Operação Economic Outcast, o Tesouro continuará a identificar e neutralizar aqueles que fornecem apoio material, tecnológico ou financeiro que permita ao regime iraniano sustentar suas atividades terroristas”, afirmou o secretário do Tesouro, Scott Bessent. “O Tesouro não tolerará qualquer apoio ao regime e continuará a identificar, expor e isolar aqueles que facilitam as ações do Irã.” O Tesouro afirmou que as sanções visam enfraquecer a capacidade de Teerã de reconstituir seus programas de armamento, ao mesmo tempo em que aumentam os custos para aqueles que apoiam seus esforços de aquisição.

item.title: Goolsbee de la Fed: inflación alta durante tanto tiempo es "jugar con fuego"
item.description: El presidente de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmó el martes que permitir que la inflación se mantenga por encima del objetivo durante cinco años y medio es "jugar con fuego", y señaló que la Fed podría verse obligada a responder a una perturbación de la oferta con efectos duraderos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, afirmó el martes que permitir que la inflación se mantenga por encima del objetivo durante cinco años y medio es "jugar con fuego", y señaló que la Fed podría verse obligada a responder a una perturbación de la oferta con efectos duraderos. "Es una situación desagradable (...) pero creo que tenemos que plantearnos responder a esas perturbaciones persistentes", afirmó el funcionario. Goolsbee señaló que es uno de los responsables de la política monetaria de la Fed más optimistas en lo que respecta a sus expectativas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés, pero antes de recortarlas "tenemos que obtener pruebas de que la inflación está volviendo a bajar, de que estos factores que se supone que son temporales están, de hecho, desapareciendo".

item.title: US drug lobby group PhRMA names former House leader Cantor as CEO
item.description: The US pharmaceutical lobby group Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America said on Tuesday it had named former US House Majority Leader Eric Cantor as its next president and chief executive officer.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US pharmaceutical lobby group Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America said on Tuesday it had named former US House Majority Leader Eric Cantor as its next president and chief executive officer. Cantor, who served in the US House of Representatives from 2000 to 2014, will take over on November 9, PhRMA said. He succeeds [USN:L4N40R1K5 TEXT:"Stephen J. Ubl"], who has led the organization since 2015, a period in which the pharmaceutical industry faced pressure from US administrations and lawmakers over prescription drug pricing, market access and regulation. PhRMA credited Cantor with backing the Medicare Part D prescription drug program, rare pediatric disease research funding and the 21st Century Cures Act during his time in Congress. Rob Davis, PhRMA board chair and CEO of Merck (MRK.N) , said in a statement that Cantor had experience in business, policy and politics. Ubl will remain as a strategic adviser until mid-January 2027 to assist with the transition.

item.title: US appeals court mulls contempt probe over Trump deportation flights
item.description: A US Justice Department lawyer asked an appeals court on Tuesday to terminate a judge's inquiry into whether Trump administration officials willfully violated a judicial order directing them to stop deportation flights of Venezuelan immigrants to El Salvador.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: A US Justice Department lawyer asked an appeals court on Tuesday to terminate a judge's inquiry into whether Trump administration officials willfully violated a judicial order directing them to stop deportation flights of Venezuelan immigrants to El Salvador. The three-hour oral argument was the latest development in a long-running standoff between President Donald Trump and US District Judge James Boasberg, who has sought to determine why his order was ignored, in a dispute that has become a test of the judiciary's power to investigate executive branch decision-making. DOJ attorney Brett Shumate told the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit during an oral argument in Washington that the criminal contempt probe by Boasberg was "unlawful, unnecessary, and futile." "The district court judge here is going beyond the judicial role," Shumate added. A three-judge D.C. Circuit panel [USN:L1N40X0ST TEXT:"blocked"] Boasberg's contempt probe in a 2-1 ruling earlier this year, but all 11 of the sitting judges on the intermediate court voted to rehear the case. The prominent appeals court has seven Democratic appointees and four Republican appointees. Some of the judges on Tuesday appeared skeptical of Shumate's arguments, saying Boasberg had properly invoked a federal rule of criminal procedure that allows a judge to investigate defiance of a court order and refer the matter for prosecution. Circuit Judge J. Michelle Childs, an appointee of Democratic President Joe Biden , said Boasberg was simply conducting "fact-finding to know what happened and know why there was a violation of the district court's order, oral and written." "The district court has to find out what happened and who was in the room providing the advice," said Circuit Judge Patricia Millett, who was appointed by Democratic President Barack Obama. The dispute arose as part of a lawsuit brought by the American Civil Liberties Union on behalf of Venezuelan men deported by the Trump administration under the Alien Enemies Act, with the plaintiffs arguing that the administration acted unlawfully with the deportation flights. The 1798 law, which has been invoked rarely in US history, gives presidents broad powers to detain and deport non-citizens. The Venezuelan men at the center of the litigation were [USN:L6N3TF0MG TEXT:"released"] from a Salvadoran prison last year and returned to Venezuela as part of a US-brokered prisoner swap. Boasberg concluded last year that the administration appeared to have acted "in bad faith" when it hurriedly assembled three deportation flights at the same time that he was conducting emergency court proceedings to assess the legality of the effort. The judge sought testimony from a high-ranking Justice Department lawyer, as well as a former department attorney who became a whistleblower. In the 2-1 ruling issued in April, the three-judge panel said Boasberg's request had encroached on "the autonomy of the executive branch" and "proposes to probe high-level Executive Branch deliberations about matters of national security and diplomacy." ACLU lawyer Lee Gelernt said during the hearing that Boasberg had acted courageously and refused to allow the executive branch to thumb its nose at him. "No prior DOJ or administrator has ever taken these kinds of egregious actions and been so disrespectful to the judiciary," Gelernt said. "If you don't uphold what this district court did, it will send a horrible message," he said.

item.title: UK's Burnham restores some hope, but near-term fixes prove elusive
item.description: Andy Burnham has restored some hope to his governing Labour Party with his vision for Britain, but how the new prime minister makes it a reality remains something of a mystery for businesses, lawmakers and even his most vocal supporters.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Piper, Andrew Macaskill, Alistair Smout
item.content:encoded: [USN:L6N43M0R2 TEXT:"Andy Burnham"] has restored some hope to his governing Labour Party with his vision for Britain, but how the new prime minister makes it a reality remains something of a mystery for businesses, lawmakers and even his most vocal supporters. At the Labour Party's annual conference in the northwestern English city of Liverpool, the mood was much more upbeat than the last two years of [USN:L8N41P1MT TEXT:"Keir Starmer"]'s administration but there were nagging questions. It remains unclear when Burnham will plot a detailed route and allocate the funds to become the "[USN:L1N43M05W TEXT:"circuit-breaker"]" for Britain's recently unstable politics. After promising to ease cost-of-living pressures and to spur economic growth through reindustrialisation and devolving power to the regions, there is little detail on how Burnham will fund and implement his feel-good agenda in the near term, companies and lawmakers say. They say he is more focused on the future, specifically after the next national election, due in mid-2029. Even his [USN:L1N45L05W TEXT:"first conference speech"] as prime minister, in which he offered an "honest conversation" on the deepest problems afflicting Britain and the trade-offs involved in tackling them, posed more questions than answers on immediate policy decisions. Burnham himself concedes he is boxed in by Starmer's earlier election promises, limiting not only his room to raise funds for his more ambitious aims before the next national election, but also preventing him from bringing in his own agenda. CONFERENCE LACKED DETAILED POLICIES, SAYS BUSINESS EXEC "The whole conference feels like it is in a haze of dope," said one business executive, speaking on condition of anonymity. "It is nice to be here. But it feels like everything is moving slowly." "The frustrating thing is some big ideas are being thrown about, but we don't know enough about how they are going to work." Companies, which paid about £6,000 ($7,925) to attend Labour's business day and the wider conference, and lawmakers, nervously eyeing opinion polls, want answers — how will the government cut energy costs, borrowing and welfare, and is there money to spend on defence, health and education before the next election. Burnham has promised to set out a 10-year plan later in the year, and has pushed back one major commitment — [USN:L6N45J04E TEXT:"the reform of social care"] — saying he would only present proposals at the next election, due by mid-2029. But after offering some short-term "breathing space" to Britons struggling with cost-of-living pressures, Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade has failed so far to offer, particularly to businesses, a blueprint of the government's investment strategy and its plans to deliver lower costs. The scale of the problems facing Britain has created some sympathy for Burnham, the former mayor who had been in parliament just a month when he became prime minister in July, after Starmer resigned earlier than expected. Alex Sobel, a Labour lawmaker, told Reuters Burnham had been dealt some of the trickiest challenges of any prime minister in modern history, including the rise of AI and wars in Iran and Ukraine pushing up Britain's energy prices. "You can't say you have had three months, and everything should be sorted by now," he said. POLL BOOST MIGHT QUICKLY DISAPPEAR, SAYS POLLSTER However, that understanding has its limits and the bounce in the opinion polls since Burnham took power could soon disappear. John Curtice, Britain's best-known pollster, said Burnham's five-point bounce was very similar to that enjoyed by former Labour Prime Minister Gordon Brown and former Conservative Prime Minister Boris Johnson when they took on their roles mid-term. Both lost their jobs about three years later. "Things are better, but the party needs to do much more to win the next election," Curtice said. That means supporting businesses still angered by the tax and wage increases brought in by Starmer, and offering a clear signal about which sectors will benefit from government spending so they can increase investment. One attendee of Labour's business day on Monday said while the access to ministers was the best they had ever had, the real test would be the budget and the 10-year plan. They remain desperate for policy details. But Burnham must also convince voters he can ease cost-of-living pressures such as energy bills over the long term, start a mass house-building programme and deliver higher defence spending and jobs, all without diverting spending on Britain's struggling public services, such as health. Businesses and lawmakers hope for more clarity in finance minister John Healey's October 28 budget, although his conference speech suggesting it would be business as usual made some worried that he was not yet ready to grasp the nettle. "The grit is going to come," said Claire Ainsley, director of the Project on Center-Left Renewal at the Progressive Policy Institute and a former Starmer adviser. "The things that it's going to take to reboot the economy are not necessarily the things that Labour members want to do." At least eight Labour lawmakers canvassed by Reuters said that if the government fails to deliver, that could hand power to the populist Reform UK party, led by Brexit campaigner Nigel Farage. The removal of Starmer for the more popular Burnham would have been all for nothing, one said. "We have to deliver. We have no choice," said Labour lawmaker Chris Curtis. "That is why we have to be bold and come up with solutions to those challenges."

item.title: Preso em um inferno após ataque russo, cientista ucraniano teve que escalar para se salvar
item.description: Ihor Malchevsky concentrou-se exclusivamente em sua família enquanto espreitava pela beirada da janela de seu escritório no terceiro andar, com uma espessa fumaça preta subindo atrás de si após um drone russo se chocar contra o prédio histórico, incendiando-o.
item.dc:creator: Daria Smetanko
item.content:encoded: Ihor Malchevsky concentrou-se exclusivamente em sua família enquanto espreitava pela beirada da janela de seu escritório no terceiro andar, com uma espessa fumaça preta subindo atrás de si após um drone russo se chocar contra o prédio histórico, incendiando-o. “Meus pensamentos estavam voltados para apenas uma coisa: como me salvar dessa situação”, disse o homem de 69 anos, vice-chefe de departamento da Academia Nacional de Ciências da Ucrânia, no centro de Kiev, atingida na segunda-feira. Malchevsky concentrou-se em sua esposa, seus dois filhos adultos e seus sete netos. Seu medo de altura não o impediu de se equilibrar do lado de fora da janela para fugir da intensa fumaça e das chamas violentas. Imagens de Malchevsky e de um colega presos no prédio em chamas, construído na era czarista, alimentaram uma nova onda de indignação diante da escalada dos ataques russos à capital ucraniana, Kiev, e a outras cidades. Nas últimas semanas, Moscou ampliou seus ataques fatais para atingir a logística de consumo, empresas e data centers. A Ucrânia atacou infraestruturas de petróleo e de defesa na Rússia, assim como varejistas online. O ataque de segunda-feira, que matou uma pessoa e feriu várias outras, foi mais um de uma série crescente de ataques diurnos ao centro de Kiev, utilizando drones a jato desenvolvidos pela Rússia para superar as defesas aéreas ucranianas. CENAS CAÓTICAS Em entrevista à Reuters um dia depois do ataque, Malchevsky relembrou os momentos caóticos após o drone se chocar contra o edifício amarelo ornamentado, a poucos passos da Ópera Nacional e da embaixada alemã. “Nos primeiros segundos você não entende nada -- depois a mente entra em ação e começa a analisar o que aconteceu”, disse em uma entrevista dele, nos arredores de Kiev. Lá embaixo, sirenes e alarmes de carros soavam enquanto transeuntes gritavam e as chamas rugiam pelo prédio. Após momentos tensos agarrado à lateral do prédio, enquanto dezenas de curiosos observavam prendendo a respiração, Malchevsky desceu cautelosamente por uma escada fornecida pelas equipes de resgate. Praticamente ileso, o pacato Malchevsky chegou à calçada e se sentou, ainda atordoado, em um parque do outro lado da rua, onde bebeu água em grandes goles para aliviar os efeitos da fumaça na garganta. Familiares correram para o local após Malchevsky ligar para eles. Sua filha, Kateryna Moskaliuk, de 37 anos, relembrou o momento em que bateu os olhos em seu pai após o ataque, coberto de fuligem. Ela sorriu aliviada, mas expressou consternação pelas inúmeras outras famílias ucranianas afetadas por mais de quatro anos de guerra. “Para que serve tudo isso?”, perguntou Moskaliuk. Os ucranianos esperam mais um inverno de ataques russos violentos à rede de energia do país, em meio à escassez de suprimentos essenciais para a defesa aérea. Malchevsky -- cujos netos, brincando, o compararam ao “Homem-Aranha” depois de verem o vídeo no YouTube -- disse que a Ucrânia deve seguir lutando para enfraquecer a Rússia, apesar das tentativas de retomada das negociações de paz apoiadas pelos Estados Unidos. Uma autoridade norte-americana afirmou nesta terça-feira que Kirill Dmitriev, o enviado do presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, teve conversas “construtivas” com seus homólogos norte-americanos.

item.title: Justice Department charges Venezuelan man shot by ICE officer in Austin
item.description: A Venezuelan man shot by a federal immigration agent on September 20 in Austin, Texas, appeared in federal court on Tuesday after being charged with assaulting, resisting, interfering, and impeding a federal officer, the Justice Department said in a press release.
item.dc:creator: Julia Harte
item.content:encoded: A Venezuelan man [USN:L6N45E0PF TEXT:"shot by a federal immigration agent"] on September 20 in Austin, Texas, appeared in federal court on Tuesday after being charged with assaulting, resisting, interfering, and impeding a federal officer, the Justice Department said in a press release. The complaint against Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, citing footage from a camera worn by one of the ICE officers who pulled him over that day, says that when they asked him to step out of his car, Garces Perez drove away, striking one officer in the torso with his car’s side mirror. The video has not been released publicly. That officer, who was not wearing a camera, chased Garces Perez down in his car and soon caught up with him, according to the complaint, which was filed on Monday in US District Court for the Western District of Texas. At that point, Garces Perez tried to drive into the officer, who fired on him with his pistol, the officer alleges in the complaint. Publicly available videos of the incident do not show the shooting, but do show Garces Perez injured in the car afterward. Garces Perez told the DHS official investigating the case that he was shot after an officer drove his SUV into his car, spinning it around, according to the complaint. Garces Perez's attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch said in an Instagram post on Sunday that her client still has the bullet in his body and a fractured clavicle, and that [USN:L6N45G13E TEXT:"his supporters"] are concerned he could experience sepsis and permanent damage if he does not get surgery soon. The Department of Homeland Security has said he is receiving adequate medical care. While the Trump administration has brought criminal charges against at least 851 people for attacking or impeding federal officers, a [USN:L6N43V0Z5 TEXT:"Reuters review of federal court records"] in July found that 31% of the completed cases had ended in dismissal, compared to the 8% dismissal rate of all federal criminal cases. Garces Perez is separately scheduled to appear before a federal immigration judge in Texas on Wednesday for a hearing on whether he can stay in the country.

item.title: US sanctions 10 over allegedly procuring weapons for Iran
item.description: The United States has sanctioned 10 individuals and entities, including some based in China, Hong Kong and Pakistan, saying they helped Iran procure weapons and components, the US Treasury Department said Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States has sanctioned 10 individuals and entities, including some based in China, Hong Kong and Pakistan, saying they helped Iran procure weapons and components, the US Treasury Department said Tuesday. The sanctions are part of the Trump administration's effort to isolate Iran economically and force it to negotiate an end to the US-Iran war that began in February. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said: “Treasury will not tolerate any support to the regime and will continue to identify, expose, and isolate Iran’s enablers.” Treasury said the sanctions were aimed at degrading Tehran's ability to reconstitute its weapons programs, while increasing the costs for those who supported its procurement efforts. Those targeted in Tuesday's sanctions announcement include: Seyyed Asghar Alizadeh Tabatabai, a Beijing-based representative of Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics agency, who Treasury said had coordinated the procurement of finished weapons systems and dual-use components in China on Iran’s behalf. Iran-based Kavoshcom Asia R and D Group, which Treasury said had procured electronics including connectors for Iran Aircraft Manufacturing Industrial Company. Hong Kong-based EC Mojo Technology Co Limited, which Treasury said had provided electronic components in support of Kavoshcom’s procurement efforts, and EC Mojo's China-based representative Li Fen. Pakistan-based Waseem Pasha Tajammal, who serves as chairman of Cavalier Group, a privately owned defense company with locations in Pakistan and internationally. Brett Erickson, managing principal with Obsidian Risk Advisors, said the latest sanctions action would do little to impede Iran's ability to launch missiles and drones in the Strait of Hormuz. "This is optics management for the Trump administration to claim 'We're hammering them,' when the reality is we're poking them with a toothpick," he said.

item.title: ONU renova mandato da força no Haiti por seis meses após novos assassinatos cometidos por gangues
item.description: O Conselho de Segurança das Nações Unidas prorrogou nesta terça-feira, por seis meses, o mandato de uma força de segurança internacional no Haiti, destinada a combater poderosos grupos armados que assumiram o controle de grande parte do país.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Morland
item.content:encoded: O Conselho de Segurança das Nações Unidas prorrogou nesta terça-feira, por seis meses, o mandato de uma força de segurança internacional no Haiti, destinada a combater poderosos grupos armados que assumiram o controle de grande parte do país. Doze países votaram a favor da renovação do mandato da Força de Supressão de Gangues (GSF) e nenhum votou contra. Três países, no entanto, se abstiveram: China, Rússia e Paquistão, cujos representantes citaram preocupações com a insuficiência de recursos financeiros, pessoal e eficácia. A prorrogação tem como objetivo garantir a segurança antes da primeira eleição no Haiti em uma década, prevista para dezembro. Grupos armados continuam a controlar grandes partes do país caribenho, apesar das sucessivas mobilizações internacionais, e a força tem enfrentado dificuldades para mobilizar tropas suficientes para cumprir seu mandato. O Haiti, cujos líderes solicitaram pela primeira vez apoio internacional em segurança em 2022, havia instado as nações a renovarem o mandato da força, que atualmente está com menos de 30% do efetivo previsto. O embaixador dos EUA na ONU, Mike Waltz, representando um dos países que propôs a moção, afirmou que cerca de 1.500 soldados da GSF estão atualmente mobilizados no Haiti. Waltz disse que os 4.000 restantes devem chegar nos próximos meses. “Sete missões foram dedicadas ao Haiti nas últimas décadas e, obviamente, com sucesso limitado”, declarou Waltz. “Estamos tentando fazer algo genuinamente diferente.” A votação ocorreu poucas horas depois que membros de gangues na região do celeiro do Haiti incendiaram casas e mataram pelo menos 11 pessoas, no que um prefeito local descreveu como retaliação após uma unidade da GSF ter matado três membros de gangues durante uma operação contra pedágios ilegais. Há um mês, outro massacre na cidade de Kenscoff, situada na encosta perto da capital, deixou pelo menos 47 mortos e cerca de 50 sequestrados. A GSF foi lançada há um ano, depois que a missão anterior, liderada pelo Quênia, também enfrentou dificuldades para atingir seus objetivos com contribuições voluntárias. Suas tropas se retiraram no início deste ano. O mandato foi renovado até 31 de março de 2027. O Haiti tem eleições marcadas para 13 de dezembro, e os resultados finais devem ser divulgados em 7 de março. Sucessivos governos de transição vêm adiando as eleições há muito tempo devido ao agravamento da insegurança, o que já forçou cerca de 1,5 milhão de pessoas a fugir de suas casas.

item.title: Fed's Williams sees no urgency for next Fed rate hike
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said on Tuesday the U.S. central bank has time to weigh the data before deciding when to hike interest rates again, in remarks that said one more increase is likely before the year ends.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said on Tuesday the U.S. central bank has time to weigh the data before deciding when to hike interest rates again, in remarks that said one more increase is likely before the year ends. “With the policy action we took at our September meeting, there is no need for urgency,” Williams said in the text of a speech prepared for delivery before an audience at the University of Buffalo, in Buffalo, New York. Watching incoming data before deciding what's next “should provide greater clarity” on how the economy is performing, Williams said. “If the economy evolves in a manner broadly consistent with my forecast, one further upward adjustment of the federal funds target range may be appropriate late this year to support a timelier return of inflation to target,” Williams said, while adding “that is just my forecast, and time — and the totality of the data — will tell.” Williams' pointed comments on the outlook for rates come as financial markets are pricing for the Fed to follow the September rate hike, which lifted the Fed’s overnight target rate range by a quarter percentage point to between 3.75% and 4%, with more increases as the year moves to a close. Futures markets see a strong chance the Fed will hike rates at its October meeting, a notion that Williams appeared to push back on. In his remarks, Williams said with the economy growing robustly and the job market holding in, price pressures can now be the main focus for monetary policy. “It is imperative that we return inflation to our 2% target on a sustained basis,” Williams said. “To do so, we must make certain that adverse inflationary disturbances do not become entrenched, and that any second-round effects on inflation remain muted.” The Fed is raising rates to deal with inflation pressures that have overshot its 2% target for over half a decade. Those pressures have worsened this year on President Donald Trump’s trade tariffs and surging energy prices tied to the war in the Middle East. Fed officials are increasingly worried inflation will not get back to target in a timely fashion and that action is needed to ensure that the public doesn’t shift toward accepting persistently high inflation as normal. Williams noted in his remarks that artificial intelligence investment is also helping to drive up price pressures, while adding tariff-related pressures have largely abated so long as the president doesn’t resort to fresh import tax increases. Williams said he sees inflation ending the year around 3.5% as price pressures ease next year on the way toward getting inflation back to target in 2028. The official also said in his remarks that he sees growth at 2.25% this year and noted that immigration factors and an aging workforce, coupled with modest productivity levels, limit how high growth can get. Williams also said that he sees the unemployment rate at 4% next year.

item.title: India's Inox Clean Energy files for $1 billion IPO
item.description: India's Inox Clean Energy filed for an initial public offering worth up to 100 billion rupees ($1.04 billion), draft papers showed on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Inox Clean Energy (INOC.NS) filed for an initial public offering worth up to 100 billion rupees ($1.04 billion), draft papers showed on Tuesday. The energy renewable producer plans to issue about 80 billion rupees worth of new shares and a 20-billion-rupee offer for sale by existing shareholders. Inox Clean Energy had [USN:L4N3T80NR TEXT:"filed"] IPO draft papers with the country's markets regulator via the confidential route last year. The company had [USN:L4N42C0YZ TEXT:"acquired"] Vena Energy India's 6-gigawatt renewable energy portfolio, bolstering its operating capacity and project pipeline in June. The firm, part of the chemicals and renewables conglomerate INOXGFL Group, aims to have 10 gigawatt of renewable power generation capacity and 11 gigawatt of solar manufacturing capacity by FY 2028. ($1 = 95.9800 Indian rupees)

item.title: EXCLUSIVE-アンソロピック、自律型ＡＩ「暴走」の法的リスク指摘＝ＩＰＯ目録見書
item.description:
Echo Wang Jody Godoy
[２９日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックは、自律型エ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE-アンソロピック、自律型ＡＩ「暴走」の法的リスク指摘＝ＩＰＯ目録見書 2:44 配信

9月17日、サンフランシスコで開催されたテクノロジー・サミットで撮影。 REUTERS/Carlos Barria

Echo Wang　Jody Godoy

[２９日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックは、自律型エージェントの予期せぬ「暴走」を巡り、法的枠組みが不確実な中、顧客やユーザーから法的請求を受ける可能性があるとの認識を示した。ロイターが入手した同社の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）目論見書で明らかになった。

アンソロピックは、ＡＩの 「自律的な機能は危害が生じるリスクを高める恐れがある。エラーやミスアライメント（意図との不一致）、セキュリティー上の悪用が現実世界への影響につながる可能性があるためだ」と説明。データ削除や金融取引といった、取り返しのつかない行動の可能性を例として挙げた。

自律型エージェントの行動を巡る法的請求については、契約で定められるアンソロピックの責任制限が「執行可能でも十分でもない可能性がある」と指摘。既存の法律がＡＩエージェントにどのように適用されるかは「未解決の問題で、アンソロピックを重大かつ予測困難な法的請求にさらす可能性がある」との認識を示した。

さらに、安全対策を講じているものの、同社のＡＩモデルがこれまでに「自傷行為や他者への暴力、その他の有害な結果につながり得る方法」で利用された事例があったと指摘した。

ＡＩエージェントによる外部システムへの不正侵入事案が相次ぐ中、被害が発生した場合の責任の所在を巡る議論が広がっている。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か コラム：米アップル、ＥＶ断念でもＡＩによる収益化期待揺るがず コラム：ＡＩで相互依存強める新興企業と巨大ＩＴ 最終更新: 9/30(水) 2:44 ロイター

item.title: Goldman succession offers less drama but more risk
item.description: A decision to name John Waldron as the next CEO of the investment bank would be an orderly and low-key way to replace boss David Solomon. Compared with the fuzzy leadership plans of JPMorgan and Bank of America, it’s a welcome change. Yet the clarity doubles the key-man hazard.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Gandel
item.content:encoded: The king of Wall Street is sending a signal who is likely to take its throne next. The board of Goldman Sachs (GS.N) is nearing a decision to name John Waldron the firm’s next chief executive, according to the Wall Street Journal. Current boss David Solomon is expected to leave the top job as soon as the end of next year. A drama-free and smooth succession would stand in contrast to rivals, especially JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) and Bank of America (BAC.N) . But the clarity, along with a lengthy hand off, could also increase Goldman’s key-man risk. The investment bank had its share of messy leadership transitions. Former Goldman chief Henry Paulson, for instance, emerged as the sole head of the bank after engineering a boardroom coup while his predecessor and then co-CEO Jon Corzine was away on a ski trip. Solomon’s hunt for his replacement has been the opposite. Waldron, who currently serves as chief operating officer, has long been viewed as his heir apparent and is one of his closest allies. Like Solomon, he rose through investment banking. Goldman further showed its hand last year by awarding Waldron an $80 million retention package. It stands in contrast to competitors. At JPMorgan, boss Jamie Dimon’s lengthy tenure has fueled years of speculation about who will replace him. The prolonged process has coincided with the departures of several senior executives once viewed as fits for the corner office. Among them are Bill Winters, now chief executive of Standard Chartered and Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf. JPMorgan recently elevated Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to co-presidents, but the ultimate succession picture remains unsettled. Even an orderly changing of the guard comes with potential drawbacks, however. Solomon is likely to stay on as executive chair for as long as two years, according to the Journal. Extended overlap periods can create complications. Walt Disney (DIS.N) head Bob Iger moved to a similar role, a problem for his successor Bob Chapek. Morgan Stanley’s (MS.N) transfer of power with James Gorman, who left the chair role after a year, provides a more attractive template. Just a few years ago, Solomon was under pressure as Goldman’s consumer-banking expansion stumbled. Nonetheless, he has refocused on the investment bank's core strengths and rewarded shareholders. The stock price has quadrupled under Solomon, besting the 52% and 112% returns of his predecessors Lloyd Blankfein and Paulson. A strong performance and solid transition plan put Goldman in a rarefied league. Follow Stephen Gandel on LinkedIn and X . The board of Goldman Sachs has talked about a plan to replace its current Chief Executive David Solomon with Chief Operating Officer John Waldron as early as next year, the Wall Street Journal reported on September 28 citing sources familiar with the matter. Solomon, who was named chief executive in 2018, may remain chair after stepping down. CONTEXT-NEWS

FAST

NEW YORK, Sept 29 : Kalshi is in advanced discussions to raise about $1 billion in fresh funding from existing and new investors, including Tiger Global Management and Dragoneer Investment Group, according to people familiar with the matter, as the prediction markets exchange looks to cement its lead over arch-rival Polymarket. The fresh capital raise is expected to be finalized in the coming weeks and will value Kalshi at about $40 billion, the sources said, requesting anonymity as the discussions are confidential. It comes on the heels of a $1 billion fundraise in May that valued the firm at $22 billion.  Sequoia Capital, which is an existing investor, is in talks to lead the latest funding round with Wellington Management, the sources said. The Information reported Sequoia and Wellington's discussions in August. Alfred Lin, one of the co-leaders at Sequoia, currently sits on Kalshi's five-member board of directors. The details of Tiger Global and Dragoneer's involvement, as well as the size of the latest fundraise, have not been previously reported.  Representatives for Kalshi and Tiger Global declined to comment. Sequoia, Wellington, and Dragoneer did not respond to requests for comment.

The funding talks come as New York-based Kalshi looks to make an ambitious push to broaden its platform to go beyond its prediction markets roots that spanned sports betting to election outcomes, and become a one-stop trading platform for a wide array of asset classes that is starting to compete with traditional exchange heavyweights, like CME Group and Intercontinental Exchange, the parent of the New York Stock Exchange. Over the course of the past year, Kalshi has also leapfrogged its nearest competitor Polymarket and grabbed market share at the expense of its crosstown rival, according to data from Dune Analytics, as the latter has been beset with struggles around the launch of its US platform and an investigation from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).  Polymarket, which counts Intercontinental Exchange among its biggest backers, is currently in separate discussions to raise $1 billion in fresh capital, according to people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg reported on Polymarket's funding talks earlier.  Kalshi was founded in 2018 by Massachusetts Institute of Technology alumni Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara. The company, which is regulated by the CFTC, was seeded out of a startup accelerator program run by Y Combinator, one of Silicon Valley's most prominent backers of early-stage ventures.  Kalshi has recently held early discussions on a potential initial public offering in the coming years, according to the sources and a recent interview with CNBC by Mansour.  Chase Coleman's Tiger Global has a deep history in the venture capital landscape and pioneered the crossover investing model, having backed several high-profile companies over the past two decades, including OpenAI, ByteDance, Revolut, and Flipkart. More recently, the firm raised a $2.2 billion venture fund, the Private Investment Partners 16 fund and is in the process of raising its PIP 17 fund, as part of a strategy to ratchet up its venture capital bets following an industry-wide downturn during a two-year period from 2022. Tiger Global currently has assets under management of about $60 billion.  San Francisco, California-based Dragoneer is a prominent technology-focused investment firm, which has backed the likes of OpenAI and SpaceX in recent years.  As prediction markets are fast becoming alternative venues for traders to place bets on big US names like Nvidia and Apple, they are also starting to raise concerns about investor protection and market oversight, Reuters reported earlier in September. Several lawmakers, including US Senator Adam Schiff, a California Democrat, have recently raised concerns about the burgeoning growth of prediction markets.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Brasil abre 165.827 vagas formais de trabalho em agosto, acima do esperado
item.description: O Brasil abriu 165.827 vagas formais de trabalho em agosto, melhor desempenho em cinco meses, mostraram dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged) divulgados nesta terça-feira pelo Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Brasil abriu 165.827 vagas formais de trabalho em agosto, melhor desempenho em cinco meses, mostraram dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged) divulgados nesta terça-feira pelo Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego. O resultado do mês passado foi fruto de 2.294.563 admissões e 2.128.736 desligamentos e ficou acima da expectativa de economistas apontada em pesquisa da Reuters de criação líquida de 97.826 vagas. (BRPROL=ECI) O saldo de agosto foi o maior desde março, quando houve abertura líquida de 228.133 vagas, e também ficou acima do número de agosto do ano passado, com 154.683 postos. No acumulado do ano até agosto, foram abertas 1.134.033 vagas, o resultado mais baixo para o período desde 2020, marcado pela pandemia da Covid-19, quando houve fechamento de 1.075.273 postos. Os cinco grupamentos de atividades econômicas registraram saldos positivos de vagas em agosto. O setor de serviços, como de costume, liderou a abertura de vagas, com 110.346 postos, seguido por construção (20.848 postos), indústria (16.613 postos), comércio (16.565) e agropecuária (1.452 postos). No total, o estoque de empregos com carteira assinada no Brasil totalizou 48.244.696 em agosto. Dados do IBGE [USN:L1N45L0EI TEXT:"mostraram"] mais cedo nesta terça-feira que a taxa de desemprego no país ficou em 5,3% nos três meses até agosto, menor nível para o período da série, iniciada em 2012.

item.title: US appeals court upholds Thomson Reuters' landmark win in AI training lawsuit
item.description: A US appeals court on Tuesday upheld a ruling for information services company Thomson Reuters in its copyright dispute with former legal-research rival Ross Intelligence over Ross' alleged misuse of copyrighted material to train an AI-powered legal search engine.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: A US appeals court on Tuesday upheld a ruling for information services company Thomson Reuters (TRI.TO) in its copyright dispute with former legal-research rival Ross Intelligence over Ross' alleged misuse of copyrighted material to train an AI-powered legal search engine. The Philadelphia-based 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals rejected Ross' argument that its search engine made fair use of material from Thomson Reuters' Westlaw platform, a first-of-its-kind ruling by a US appeals court in a wave of high-stakes copyright cases over AI training. The appeals court's reasoning for its decision is currently sealed. Spokespeople and an attorney for Ross did not immediately respond to requests for comment. A Thomson Reuters spokesperson said the company was pleased with the ruling and "firmly believes that respecting copyright is essential for fostering innovation while protecting the intellectual property that fuels fiduciary-grade AI solutions." Thomson Reuters is the parent company of Reuters News. Thomson Reuters' 2020 lawsuit accused legal research company Ross Intelligence of copying Westlaw's "headnotes," which summarize points of law in court opinions. It accused Ross of misusing thousands of headnotes to train its competing AI-based legal search engine. Ross shut down its platform in 2021, citing the costs of Thomson Reuters' litigation. Authors, news outlets, music labels and others have filed [USN:L6N3XM122 TEXT:"dozens of lawsuits"] against tech companies over the unauthorized use of copyrighted works to train AI systems. Thomson Reuters' case is the first copyright dispute over AI training to be heard by a US appeals court, though unlike those disputes, Thomson Reuters' case does not involve generative AI -- artificial intelligence that creates new content. Ross allegedly used Thomson Reuters' headnotes to train its search engine to identify relevant court opinions in response to user queries. The company argued that its AI training made fair use of the headnotes, raising a pivotal defense for legal disputes over AI training. Tech companies have argued that generative AI systems make fair use of the copyrighted material they are trained on by transforming it into something new, while copyright owners say the companies use their work to generate competing content that threatens their livelihoods. A federal judge in Delaware federal court [USN:L1N3P20P5 TEXT:"rejected Ross' fair use defense"] last year, prompting Ross' appeal. "Ross took the headnotes to make it easier to develop a competing legal research tool," the judge said. "So Ross’s use is not transformative."

item.title: Canadian institutions should not fear using liquidity facility, says Bank of Canada
item.description: The Bank of Canada on Tuesday urged financial institutions to use its Standing Liquidity Facility for overnight liquidity when needed without worrying that it might be seen as a sign of stress.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Canada on Tuesday urged financial institutions to use its Standing Liquidity Facility for overnight liquidity when needed without worrying that it might be seen as a sign of stress. In a joint statement with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, Canada's banking regulator, the BoC said SLF advances were considered normal. The statement was released at the same time as remarks by Deputy Governor Toni Gravelle on the bank's efforts to strengthen repo market operations. "We view an institution's use of the SLF for overnight liquidity as a normal part of day-to-day liquidity management, not as an exceptional event or a sign of stress," Gravelle told a Bloomberg conference in New York. The SLF is the BoC's standing lending facility for participants in Canada’s high-value payment system, Lynx. It provides financial institutions who are a part of the central bank's payment system with fully secured intraday and overnight credit. This helps institutions settle payments during the day and at the end-of-day operations. Institutions usually settle their end-of-day payments from reserves they are holding as a buffer - money which could otherwise be released into the market, helping payment system efficiency. The BoC and OSFI consider SLF use by Lynx participants to be consistent with routine liquidity management activities, the central bank said, adding the participants can use the facility as needed. Gravelle said the BoC was working to update and strengthen its repo clearing infrastructure as it starts using a new tri-party platform which will help develop the term repo market and attract new participants such as large corporate treasuries. Repo markets are crucial for the functioning of government bond markets and are also an important source of short-term funding. But their size and widespread use mean they can transmit financial stress if conditions deteriorate.

item.title: White House urges EU to draw down diesel inventories, sources say
item.description: The White House has urged the European Union to draw down emergency diesel inventories in an effort to lower global prices, as President Donald Trump and his administration pursue a range of options to ease fuel costs ahead of November's midterm elections, according to two sources familiar with the effort.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: The White House has urged the European Union to draw down emergency diesel inventories in an effort to lower global prices, as President Donald Trump and his administration pursue a range of options to ease fuel costs ahead of November's midterm elections, according to two sources familiar with the effort. The White House is frustrated that some European countries have not lived up to commitments made earlier this year to tap their emergency oil and petroleum reserves to help address supply disruptions and price spikes stemming from the Iran conflict and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, according to the sources. US officials are particularly frustrated with France and Germany , which they believe have fallen short of their commitments, and have raised their concerns with the International Energy Agency, which coordinates emergency oil stockpile releases among member countries, according to the sources. Washington agreed in March to loan 172 million barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with about 30 countries in the International Energy Agency to release 400 million barrels from reserves around the world. EU countries agreed to jointly contribute 20% of the oil stocks release. In announcing a new release of oil from US reserves, Energy Secretary Chris Wright publicly pressed European countries to fulfill their commitments, saying on Tuesday that while the US and Japan were delivering on theirs, “several European member countries have released only a fraction” of the crude oil and petroleum products they had pledged. Soaring diesel prices have become a political headache for Trump and Republicans, particularly in farm states where the fuel is critical to agriculture, trucking and manufacturing. With Republicans facing pressure to address the cost-of-living squeeze before the elections, the administration is considering a range of measures to bring prices down, including encouraging foreign stockpile releases, restricting US diesel exports and working with refiners to increase domestic supplies. EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen said on Tuesday that the bloc had discussed with International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol whether to release more emergency oil stocks but had not decided whether to urge member states to do so. “We still have to have talks amongst the member states and IEA on these issues,” Jorgensen told reporters, adding that the EU had to balance the need to ease price spikes against preserving emergency stocks for potentially worse supply disruptions. The EU did not immediately respond to requests for comment on US allegations that members were not living up to commitments. The EU has not disclosed the total volumes its members have so far released, although the IEA has said EU countries' contributions will primarily take the form of refined products, rather than crude oil. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The administration’s approach to the diesel crunch remains unsettled. Trump has publicly backed a ban on US diesel exports, but administration officials have spent the past week exploring alternatives that could boost domestic supplies without imposing a blanket ban, including seeking [USN:L1N45G0Q3 TEXT:"voluntary export limits"] from refiners and allowing [USN:L1N45K0KX TEXT:"broader sales of tax-exempt red-dyed diesel"]. No final decisions have been made, according to the White House.

item.title: インフレ抑制へ追加利上げが必要になる可能性＝バーＦＲＢ理事
item.description:
Ann Saphir
［２９日 ロイター］ - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のバー理事は２９日、ＦＲＢが目標とする２％...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インフレ抑制へ追加利上げが必要になる可能性＝バーＦＲＢ理事 2:19 配信

2026年2月17日、米国ニューヨーク市で撮影。 REUTERS/Brendan McDermid/File Photo

Ann Saphir

［２９日　ロイター］ - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のバー理事は２９日、ＦＲＢが目標とする２％のインフレ率に向けた進展が「軌道から外れた」とし、追加利上げの必要性を改めて訴えた。エネルギー価格の高騰や人工知能（ＡＩ）関連投資の急増が背景にあるとした。

デトロイト経済クラブでの講演原稿によると、バー理事は「２％への適時の回帰に向けた明確な傾向は、まだ見られない」とし、インフレ率は高すぎ、これを目標に戻す上でのリスクは高まっている一方、労働市場は堅調でリスクは低下していると指摘した。

「二大責務の双方に関するリスクをより均衡の取れた形で調整できる状況にするため、政策を再調整する必要がある」と語った。

金融市場では、ＦＲＢが今月実施した利上げに続き、１０月２７─２８日の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で０．２５％ポイントの追加利上げを行うとの見方が強い。

バー理事は「私の基本シナリオでは、インフレ率を適時に目標へ低下させるため、さらなる政策調整が必要になる可能性が高い」と述べた。

２０２６年後半の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）成長率は、上半期の２％ペースから「やや加速」する見通しとした。企業投資と個人消費が労働市場を支えているという。

また、中東の紛争が世界の原油価格を押し上げているほか、ＡＩの設備投資拡大が特定のハイテク製品への需要を高め、企業・消費者向け価格を押し上げていると指摘した。

ＡＩ投資は今後１年程度、米経済活動を力強く押し上げ続ける可能性が高いとの見方を示した。一方、長期的にはＡＩが生産性の伸びを高め、インフレを伴わないより速い経済成長を可能にすると楽観しているものの、生産性向上がいつ、どのように実現するかを予測するのは難しいと述べた。

さらに、ＡＩがもたらす長期的な恩恵を実現するためには、「労働市場に深刻な短期的混乱が生じる可能性に備え、それを効果的に管理しなければならない」と語った。

ＡＩが経済やＦＲＢの適切な政策金利水準に及ぼす影響を正確に見極めるのは時期尚早としつつ、「現時点で明らかなのは、インフレ率が高すぎることだ」と強調した。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：日米欧9月同時利上げ、浮き彫りになった「日銀の弱点」＝上野泰也氏 焦点：ＦＲＢが狙う「雇用損なわない」インフレ抑制、コロナ禍後の再現なるか コラム：何が豪ドルを動かしているのか＝高島修氏 コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 コラム：ドル／円の昨年高値更新に現実味、中立金利や介入効果に注目＝内田稔氏 最終更新: 9/30(水) 2:19 ロイター

item.title: OpenAI takes on Meta with dots agent in enterprise AI push
item.description: OpenAI on Tuesday unveiled always-on agents called dots that chase user goals across apps on their own, deepening its push into the lucrative enterprise market and pitting it against Meta in the race to sell AI that can work autonomously.
item.dc:creator: Deepa Seetharaman, Aditya Soni
item.content:encoded: [USN:L4N45L1NS TEXT:"OpenAI"] on Tuesday unveiled always-on agents called dots that chase user goals across apps on their own, deepening its push into the lucrative enterprise market and pitting it against Meta (META.O) in the race to sell AI that can work autonomously. The dots agents aim to capitalize on growing demand for agents that can handle everyday work with little supervision. Interest in such tools has surged since [USN:L4N45L0QP TEXT:"Meta's Muse"] drew millions of downloads earlier this month and jolted shares of companies that investors believe could benefit or be disrupted by autonomous AI services. Instinct, the startup behind the eponymous agent, also quadrupled its valuation to $10 billion this week, a little over a month after its previous fundraise. OpenAI launched dots at its annual developer day in San Francisco on Tuesday while also touting its growing business and consumer presence, a sign that the reception for the company's Astra model has allowed it to make up ground in the AI race. It also comes a day after OpenAI shelved the release of a more powerful Astra model, saying it showed a high willingness to mislead users about its actions. The company is under scrutiny after its rogue AI agents hacked [USN:L6N45H0LE TEXT:"Hugging Face"] and an [USN:L4N45L03J TEXT:"Australian government health website"] during internal testing. Growing quickly is crucial for OpenAI's plans to spend tens of billions of dollars on AI data centers and keep pace with rivals such as Anthropic and Meta. The company, which ignited the AI boom with ChatGPT in late 2022, is also preparing for an IPO that could value it at more than $1 trillion. Rival Anthropic could be worth $2 trillion when it goes public. MANAGING EVOLVING PROJECTS "We believe (the agent) is going to feel like a whole new way to work with AI. This is the real deal version of AI that we've always imagined for ourselves," CEO Sam Altman said at the event, which had around 2,500 in-person attendees. OpenAI's live demos to show off the new capabilities, however, hit snags as the agents repeatedly failed to deliver voice updates in response to requests. "We might have some voice difficulties at the moment. Which is pretty unfortunate," Developer Experience chief Romain Huet said on stage after a command fell flat. One OpenAI employee said on X that the glitches stemmed from rolling out all the updates at once, but that OpenAI remained committed to live demos. Dots use OpenAI's advanced GPT-6 Astra model and can manage projects as they evolve, such as updating a sales proposal when customer needs change, and building a working demo for review. Users can communicate with dots on Slack and Teams, and the agents can draw on OpenAI's Codex and ChatGPT Work tools to research, analyze data, prepare documents and build software. On Tuesday, OpenAI highlighted safeguards it has built into dots. It said users could set custom rules that dictate what dots can do and when the agents should seek permission, adding that sensitive tasks such as changing passwords and permanently deleting data require explicit user consent. The company also said dots run on their own cloud computers, and that it was rolling out private intelligence tools to check for safety risks without retaining business customers' data. Several tech executives, including Palantir (PLTR.O) CEO Alex Karp, have in recent months said that businesses need certainty that AI companies are not retaining their data, especially in regulated industries such as healthcare and finance. Reuters reported on Friday that OpenAI was still working to understand the full scope of its rogue agent activity, two months after the Hugging Face hack, with the latest example coming when the startup said its agents had leaked 53 images from ChatGPT users. OpenAI reiterated on Tuesday that it does not use business customers' data to train its AI by default, and that personal-plan users could opt out of sharing conversations and dots work used for training. Weekly users of Codex and ChatGPT Work have reached more than 35 million, up from about 5 million Codex users in June, the company said Tuesday, while consumer-focused ChatGPT now has over 1.2 billion weekly users. The company is rolling out a range of new offerings including a shared workspace for business teams and AI called ChatGPT Space, the cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol model and a $500 Pro plan offering higher usage and faster performance.

item.title: 米小売り大手、値下げの動き相次ぐ ターゲットは約2000品目
item.description: [２９日 ロイター] - 米小売り大手ターゲットは２９日、家庭用品や衣料品、アクセサリーなど約２０００品目を値下げする...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米小売り大手、値下げの動き相次ぐ　ターゲットは約2000品目 2:10 配信

米ニュージャージー州にあるターゲットで2024年11月撮影。REUTERS/Siddharth Cavale

[２９日　ロイター] - 米小売り大手ターゲットは２９日、家庭用品や衣料品、アクセサリーなど約２０００品目を値下げすると発表した。ホリデー商戦を控え、ガソリン価格高騰などで消費を手控える買い物客を呼び込む狙い。同業大手のウォルマートも８月に約１万１０００品目の値下げを発表するなど、価格引き下げの動きが相次いでいる。

ターゲットは今年３月に３０００余りの品目の値下げを発表するなど、過去１年間に１万点以上の品目で実施してきたと説明している。値下げを追い風に直近３四半期の決算は好業績を維持しており、８月には通期売上高の見通しを上方修正した。マイケル・フィデルケ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が進める経営再建策が成果を挙げ始めていることが示された。

ターゲットのカーラ・シルベスター最高マーチャンダイジング責任者は「良い商品を大幅な安値で提供することが求められている」と指摘した。今回は衣料品や靴を値下げするほか、寝具の価格も引き下げるという。毎週のセールなども実施するとした。

ウォルマートは値下げの原資として関税還付金を充てると説明していた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず アングル：米企業、金利上昇で借り換え負担増大　コロナ禍調達分の満期相次ぐ コラム：米利上げでアジア株式市場に明暗、経常赤字国の打撃大きく 焦点：ＦＲＢが狙う「雇用損なわない」インフレ抑制、コロナ禍後の再現なるか アングル：欧米小売、インフレ下でも有名人起用や価格戦略で需要喚起 最終更新: 9/30(水) 2:10 ロイター

item.title: US lawmakers including Sen. Warren push energy regulators to reject acquisition of power company AES
item.description: A group of US lawmakers including Senator Elizabeth Warren asked federal energy regulators this week to reject a more than $33 billion sale of power company AES, saying it could drive up electricity bills and benefit data centers at the expense of utility customers, according to a letter seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Laila Kearney, Sumit Saha
item.content:encoded: A group of US lawmakers including Senator Elizabeth Warren asked federal energy regulators this week to reject a more than $33 billion sale of power company AES, saying it could drive up electricity bills and benefit data centers at the expense of utility customers, according to a letter seen by Reuters. U.S. electricity demand is being driven to record highs, largely by the proliferation of energy-intensive data centers, spurring a flurry of power mergers and acquisitions, some of which propose to take public electric utilities private. BlackRock's (BLK.N) Global Infrastructure Partners, alongside Swedish private equity EQT (EQTAB.ST) and other investors, agreed in March to acquire AES (AES.N) in a deal valued at about $33.4 billion including debt, making it one of the largest power sector transactions in recent years. "The private equity industry’s involvement in the public utility market has significant implications for consumers’ energy costs at a time when Americans are facing record high utility bills," said the letter dated Sept. 28, which was directed to Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Chairman Laura Swett. BlackRock declined to comment. EQT did not immediately respond to a request for comment. AES in an emailed statement said, the acquisition is not expected to impact customer rates in company's regulated utilities. "No costs associated with the acquisition — including any premium paid or transaction-related expenses — will be borne by utility ratepayers and for the Company’s electric utilities in Indiana and Ohio," it added. The sale of AES is pending approvals by FERC, which is tasked with determining whether the transaction is in the public's interest. In their letter to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Chairman Laura Swett, dated September 28, the lawmakers argued that the acquisition fails the public interest test, partially because it could increase energy costs for homes and businesses. The letter was signed by a bipartisan group of lawmakers, including Indiana representatives André Carson, a Democrat, and Victoria Spartz, a Republican, as well as Democratic Representatives Rashida Tlaib of Michigan and Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts. As part of the acquisition, publicly traded AES would become a privately held company, while utilities AES Indiana and AES Ohio would remain regulated subsidiaries. The group said that GIP generally seeks an internal rate of return of around 15% to 20%, roughly double the historical 10% median earned by regulated utilities, creating incentives to pursue higher profits by hiking electricity rates. AES has said in public filings that the deal would not raise rates at the utilities, which would continue to be state regulated and operated locally, and that the acquisition would broadly improve its access to capital to invest in critical grid infrastructure. The acquisition, the lawmakers said, could also increase the risk of "cross-subsidization" between BlackRock's utility holdings and its investments in data centers across the country. The lawmakers argued that BlackRock's growing ownership of both electric infrastructure and data centers could create incentives for utility investments that primarily benefit affiliated data centers, while leaving other customers to bear part of the costs. "Even worse, if a data center fails, customers may continue paying for the unnecessary upgrades via increased utility bills," the letter said. AES shareholders have approved the transaction and Ohio regulators approved the transfer of AES Ohio earlier this month. The parties have said the deal is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027, subject to remaining regulatory approvals, including by FERC.

item.title: Appeals court declines to pause sanctions against Trump lawyers in IRS settlement
item.description: A US appeals court declined on Tuesday to immediately block sanctions against lawyers for Donald Trump who a judge accused of misusing the court system in settling a lawsuit the Republican president filed against the Internal Revenue Service.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff
item.content:encoded: A US appeals court declined on Tuesday to immediately block sanctions against lawyers for Donald Trump who a judge accused of misusing the court system in settling a lawsuit the Republican president filed against the Internal Revenue Service. The ruling, rejecting a request made by Trump's lawyers and the Justice Department, was issued by a three-judge panel of the Atlanta-based 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals, with no dissents noted. The decision for now lets stand an order by Miami-based US District Judge Kathleen Williams concluding that Trump [USN:S0N3Y800M TEXT:"improperly filed"] a $10 billion lawsuit to [USN:L1N40Y0AR TEXT:"extract personal benefits"] from the US government, including a now-abandoned plan for a nearly $1.8 billion fund for his allies and[USN:L6N41W1AI TEXT:" protections from tax audits"]. Williams determined that the agreement was improperly collusive given that Trump, as president, controls the agencies his personal lawyers sued. The judge's order referred one of Trump's personal lawyers to Florida legal disciplinary authorities and barred any of the parties in the case — including Trump, his adult sons and his namesake company — from referring to the agreement as a court settlement or citing any of its terms in future legal proceedings. In their appeal of the judge's ruling, Trump's lawyers and the Justice Department argued that it ran afoul of the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech. The 11th Circuit panel concluded that the bar referral for one of Trump's lawyers, Alejandro Brito, was not a final order that could be appealed. The panel also determined that the judge's prohibition on Trump and his businesses referring to a settlement was sufficiently limited so as not to infringe on free speech rights. A spokesperson for Trump's legal team reiterated claims that the president's lawsuit against the IRS was an appropriate means to "hold those who wrong America and Americans accountable." A Justice Department spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump filed suit this year against the IRS, alleging the tax agency did not do enough to prevent the leak of his tax records during his first term as president. Trump and Justice Department lawyers brokered an agreement in May to dismiss his lawsuit in exchange for the IRS giving immunity to him and his businesses over past tax claims and the department creating a nearly $1.8 billion fund to compensate his allies who allege prior government mistreatment. The Justice Department scrapped plans for the fund following opposition from Democratic and Republican lawmakers. Trump's lawyers and the Justice Department "did not submit or offer any evidence to explain their litigation conduct or demonstrate that the lawsuit and the settlement were not collusive," the 11th Circuit panel stated.

item.title: US FAA hiring two Southwest Airlines employees for senior roles
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration said it hiring two Southwest Airlines employees for senior roles at the agency and is tapping a senior official at NetJets to serve as the agency's chief counsel starting next month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Federal Aviation Administration said it hiring two Southwest Airlines (LUV.N) employees for senior roles at the agency and is tapping a senior official at NetJets to serve as the agency's chief counsel starting next month. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said Chris Kelly, a senior regulatory attorney at Southwest Airlines, will join the FAA as  the new associate administrator for airports. Other changes: * Southwest senior federal affairs director Michael Ciamarra will join the FAA as assistant administrator for policy and rulemaking. * Jeff DeVore, who has been in-house counsel at NetJets, will serve as the new FAA chief counsel. * Current Chief Counsel and acting deputy administrator Liam McKenna is being named FAA Chief Strategy Officer * Bailey Wood named FAA assistant administrator for government and industry affairs, who most recently has been director of strategic communications for Vertical Aviation International.

FAST

WASHINGTON, Sept 29 : A sponsor of a bill toughen a U.S. government ban on Chinese vehicles said Tuesday talks are ongoing to ensure German automaker Mercedes-Benz is not banned from selling vehicles in the United States. The bill approved by the Senate Commerce Committee in July would ban companies with more than 15 per cent ownership by Chinese entities from selling vehicles in the United States. Mercedes-Benz has nearly 20 per cent passive ownership from Chinese entities. "What we're not going to do, obviously, is ban Mercedes-Benz vehicles in America," said Republican Bernie Moreno, adding "there's concern that can they get to 15 per cent without debilitating their company?" Moreno hopes to try to win fast-track approval for the Chinese vehicle bill this week before the Senate adjourns until November.

Source: Reuters

Exclusive-Anthropic says rogue AI agents pose uncertain legal risk for the company

People visit an Anthropic booth at Moscone Center during the Dreamforce 2026 technology summit in San Francisco, California, US, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Carlos Barria

FILE PHOTO: Anthropic logo, a keyboard, and a robotic hand in this illustration taken June 5, 2026. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

FAST

Sept 29 : Anthropic could face legal claims from customers and users over the actions of rogue artificial intelligence agents, though the legal framework is uncertain, the company said in the prospectus for its stock market debut seen by Reuters. While it gears up for what could be the largest initial public offering ever, Anthropic faces the possibility of vast unknown legal risk if its agentic AI technology - designed to maintain deep access to customers' systems and run autonomously for days at a time - goes rogue. "These autonomous capabilities could increase the potential for harm, as errors, misalignment, or security exploits may result in real-world consequences," the company said in the documents, citing the possibility of irreversible actions such as data deletion or financial transactions. While online platforms have long enjoyed immunity from content created or posted by users, that legal shield has started to crack against theories that the platforms are products that can be defective and dangerous. It is unclear whether use of AI systems would receive the same legal treatment as online platforms at all.
